# Uniform real Lipschitz surfaces on the triangular lattice

Coordinate `EN-115-000-0003-2-2026-PR-T4-UK-EX-M2-C-ML-M-0462` | `PM-232.3` | status ACTIVE | original slug `Uniform-real-Lipschitz-surfaces-on-the-triangular-lattice-October-6-2026` | date 2026-10-06 | derived from the openai/math preprint Uniform-real-Lipschitz-surfaces-on-the-triangular-lattice-October-6-2026, modified (Apache-2.0). ```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove the Gaussian free field and SLE$`_4`$ scaling limits for uniformly sampled real nearest-neighbor Lipschitz heights on the triangular lattice, resolving Schramm's Problem 2.3. On approximations of smooth simply connected domains, the centered height field converges as a random distribution to a multiple of the Dirichlet Gaussian free field. At one tuned two-arc boundary amplitude, the zero-height interface converges in uniform curve distance to chordal SLE$`_4`$. We identify the relation between the field variance and the boundary height in terms of an implicit stationary tangent-flux coefficient.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove the Gaussian free field and SLE$`_4`$ scaling limits for uniformly sampled real nearest-neighbor Lipschitz heights on the triangular lattice, resolving Schramm's Problem 2.3. On approximations of smooth simply connected domains, the centered height field converges as a random distribution to a multiple of the Dirichlet Gaussian free field. At one tuned two-arc boundary amplitude, the zero-height interface converges in uniform curve distance to chordal SLE$`_4`$. We identify the relation between the field variance and the boundary height in terms of an implicit stationary tangent-flux coefficient.

- **claim-field-and-interface-limits** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): There are constants $A>0$, $\sigma>0$, and $\lambda\in(0,1/2]$, independent of $D,a,b$, such that the model <a href="#eq:model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:model">[eq:model]</a> has $$\gamma_\delta\Longrightarrow\mathrm{SLE}_4(D;a,b),\qquad \frac{h_\delta-\mathbb Eh_\delta}{\sigma} \Longrightarrow\mathrm{GFF}_D$$ in the stated curve metric and as random distributions, respectively. The constants and limiting mean are $$\begin{aligned} v&=2/\sqrt3,&\sigma^2&=(vA)^{-1},& \lambda^2&=\frac{\pi}{8vA},\label{eq:target-constants}\\ m_D(z)&=\lambda\bigl[\omega_D(z,A_+)-\omega_D(z,A_-)\bigr].&&& \label{eq:target-mean} \end{aligned}$$ Here $\omega_D$ is harmonic measure and $A$ is the tangent-flux coefficient defined in the cell construction. The stiffness is $vA$; no elementary closed form for it is proposed.
  - Explanation: The centered real Lipschitz height field has a Dirichlet Gaussian free field limit, and the interface has a chordal scaling limit at the tuned boundary amplitude. The variance and amplitude are determined by the implicit tangent-flux coefficient.
- **claim-macroscopic-exponential-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-f-averages)): Fix $c,C>0$ and $B<\infty$. Let $R\ge1$ and let deterministic real weights $q_x$ obey $$\label{f:weights} \sum_x\|q_x\|\le C,\qquad \max_x\|q_x\|\le CR^{-2},\qquad \operatorname{supp}q\subset Q, \quad \operatorname{diam}Q\le CR,$$ where $Q$ is an ambient coordinate box. Assume either $\sum_xq_x=0$, or there is a connected set of pins $K$, of diameter at least $cR$, such that $K\cup Q$ lies in a coordinate box of diameter at most $CR$. For a sample $h$ from $\mu_b$, there are $a>0$ and $M<\infty$, depending only on $c,C,B$, such that $$\label{f:average-mgf} \mathbb E\exp\left(a\left\|\sum_xq_xh(x)\right\|\right)\le M.$$ The conclusion is uniform over mixtures of bounded pin values whenever conditioning on those values leaves exactly the specified uniform law.
  - Explanation: Spread macroscopic averages have uniform exponential moments when their additive constant is removed by cancellation or a connected pin anchor. The same estimate survives admissible mixtures.
- **claim-triangular-block-deficit** (bound, [source](#stmt-f-block)): For these fixed parameters there is $c_*>0$ such that, if $Q$ is convex-good for $h$, $s=h\|_{\partial Q}$, $\chi:\partial Q\to\mathbb R$, and both $K_Q(s+\chi)$ and $K_Q(s-\chi)$ have positive volume, then every two face centers $v,w$ satisfy $$\label{f:block-deficit} g_Q:=F_Q(s)-\tfrac12\bigl(F_Q(s+\chi)+F_Q(s-\chi)\bigr) \ge c_*\|\chi(v)-\chi(w)\|^2.$$
  - Explanation: On a convex-good block, loss of filling volume under opposite shell perturbations controls differences between their face-center values.
- **claim-zero-pinned-sparse-blocks** (bound, [source](#stmt-f-sparse)): For every $\rho>0$ the fixed parameters above and a fixed enlargement $Q_z^*$ can be chosen so that the following holds uniformly over zero-pinned finite volumes. Declare every block within a fixed block distance of a pin to be a pin block. Among the remaining blocks declare a block bad when it fails <a href="#f:near" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="f:near">[f:near]</a>, the long-distance condition <a href="#f:far" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="f:far">[f:far]</a> on $Q_z^*$, or one of the four non-tie tests. Then $$\label{f:animal} \mathbb P(A\text{ is entirely bad})\le\rho^{\|A\|}$$ for every finite set $A$ of block indices. The collar defining pin blocks contains all enlargements $Q_z^*$. Fixed finite thickenings of the bad set also satisfy such a bound with an arbitrarily small parameter, after adjusting the initial parameters.
  - Explanation: Failure of the slack and non-tie tests has an arbitrarily small animal bound. Fixed finite enlargements preserve this form of sparsity.
- **claim-stationary-step-displacement** (bound, [source](#stmt-f-step)): Let $(H_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be a stationary reversible normally reflected diffusion in a finite convex polytope, with Brownian covariance $2I$ and invariant uniform law. The same assertion holds with constant drift $b$ and invariant density proportional to $e^{b\cdot h}$. For distinct free coordinates $x_1,\ldots,x_j$, $$\label{f:step-tail} \mathbb P\left(\sup_{t\le T}\|H_t(x_i)-H_0(x_i)\|>r \text{ for all }i\right) \le\bigl(Ce^{-r^2/(CT)}\bigr)^{j/2}.$$ Thus the zero-pinned good-block conditions persist with relaxed fixed constants throughout a sufficiently short step, apart from arbitrarily sparse exceptional blocks. The same implication holds for any other stationary constrained law for which the initial block tests have the joint sparse bound.
  - Explanation: Forward and reverse Brownian martingales control joint coordinate displacement tails, so initial sparse good-block tests persist during a sufficiently short stationary step.
- **claim-sparse-hole-extension** (construction, [source](#stmt-f-hole)): Let a random bad set on the square grid satisfy <a href="#f:animal" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="f:animal">[f:animal]</a> with sufficiently small parameter. Fill the bounded complementary components of each bad star-connected cluster and retain its outermost filled hulls. A fixed layer of enlargement is allowed. There is an extension procedure which, for a field $u$ on good sites, fills each hole by its value at one surrounding good site. Here good sites lie outside the filled holes and good edges join neighboring good sites. Write $v$ for the resulting field. A hole is incident to $z$ if it contains $z$ or a neighbor of $z$; let $d_z$ be the largest diameter of an incident hole, zero if none, and put $d_e=\max(d_x,d_y)$ for $e=\{x,y\}$. Uniformly in deterministic $z$, $$\label{f:hole-tail} \mathbb P(d_z\ge r)\le Ce^{-cr}.$$ For every $1<p<2$, on a square of side $N$ with a fixed larger buffer, $$\label{f:hole-weighted} \\|\nabla v\\|_{\ell^p} \le E^{1/2} \left(\sum_e W_e^{2/(2-p)}a_e^{-p/(2-p)}\right)^{(2-p)/(2p)}, \quad W_e\le C_p(1+d_e)^{2p},$$ where $E=\sum_{e\text{ good}}a_e\|\nabla u(e)\|^2$, $a_e>0$. In particular, bounded spatial moments of sufficiently high powers of $d_e$ and $a_e^{-1}$ imply $$\label{f:hole-scaled} \\|\nabla v\\|_{\ell^p}\le C N^{2/p-1}\sqrt E.$$ If $u$ is the restriction of a globally $K$-Lipschitz field on the grid, then $\|u(z)-v(z)\|\le CK(1+d_z)$.* *For every fixed $q,D<\infty$, the spatial average of $(1+d_z)^q$ in a square of side $N$ is bounded by a deterministic constant outside an event of probability $O(N^{-D})$. In a box of side $n$, these bounds hold simultaneously on all subboxes of radius at least $n^{1/2}$, after altering the failure exponent. Filling can be chosen equivariantly under translations of the block grid. No reciprocal-weight assertion follows from sparsity alone; those moments are separate hypotheses in <a href="#f:hole-weighted" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="f:hole-weighted">[f:hole-weighted]</a>.
  - Explanation: Fill sparse holes from surrounding good sites. Rim paths control the extension gradient and its error, while separate reciprocal-weight moments remain necessary for weighted estimates.
- **claim-spread-measure-trace-average** (bound, [source](#stmt-f-trace-average)): Let $\nu$ be a positive measure of bounded mass in a square of side $O(N)$, and assume $\nu(B(x,r))\le C((r+1)/N)^\alpha$ for $0\le r\le CN$. If $1<p<2$ and $\alpha>2-p$, then $$\|\nu(v)-\nu(1)\overline v\| \le C N^{1-2/p}\\|\nabla v\\|_{\ell^p},$$ where $\overline v$ is the ordinary average over that square.
  - Explanation: A measure with controlled ball masses tests the difference between a grid field and its ordinary average through its gradient norm.
- **claim-uniform-average-coercivity** (bound, [source](#stmt-f-average-coercivity)): Suppose $X$ is globally $K$-Lipschitz on the block grid, with fixed $K$. Suppose either $u=X$, or $u=T_M(X)$ for fixed $T_M(t)=\operatorname{sign}(t)(\|t\|-M)_+$. Let $E=\sum_{e\text{ good}}\|\nabla u(e)\|^2$. For deterministic weights $w$ supported in an $O(N)$ square with $\sum\|w\|\le C$ and $\max\|w\|\le CN^{-2}$, assume either $\sum w=0$, or $u=0$ on a connected deterministic coarse pin set of diameter comparable to $N$ at distance $O(N)$. There is an event of probability at least $1/2$, determined only by the bad set, on which simultaneously for every such field $X$, $$\label{f:coercivity} \left\|\sum_z w_zX_z\right\|\le C_0+C_1\sqrt E.$$
  - Explanation: Good-edge energy controls weighted macroscopic averages simultaneously for all admissible Lipschitz fields on an event determined by the bad set.
- **claim-bounded-data-coupling** (construction, [source](#stmt-f-bounded)): There is a coupling of $h_b\sim\mu_b$ and one sample $h_0\sim\mu_0$ with $\|h_b-h_0\|\le B$ at every vertex, whenever $\|b\|\le B$. Consequently Proposition <a href="#f:averages" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:averages">2</a> holds for bounded data and their admissible mixtures.
  - Explanation: A monotone coupling compares bounded pin data with one zero-pinned sample, transferring the macroscopic moment estimate.
- **claim-small-linear-tilts** (bound, [source](#stmt-f-tilts)): Under Proposition <a href="#f:averages" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:averages">2</a>, let $Y=\sum_x b_xh(x)$, with support in an $O(R)$ box and $\|b_x\|\le cR^{-2}$. Assume its box has the specified connected pin anchor, or that $\sum_xb_x=0$. For sufficiently small fixed $c>0$, the tilted density $e^Y/\mathbb Ee^Y$ has uniformly bounded $L^2$ norm. Hence for every event $A$, $$\mathbb P_Y(A)\le C\mathbb P(A)^{1/2}.$$ All fixed moments of admissible average statistics remain bounded under this tilt, and any established arbitrary-parameter animal estimate is inherited, with a harmless constant prefactor and changed parameter.
  - Explanation: Sufficiently small anchored or zero-mass tilts have bounded square-integrable density and preserve admissible moments and sparse-event estimates.
- **claim-strict-sign-interval-filling** (construction, [source](#stmt-f-strict-filling)): In a finite patch, prescribe arbitrary shell values, interior fixed pins in $[-1/2,1/2]$, and intervals containing zero at any other prescribed vertices. The intervals may be one-sided or of the form $[0,\varepsilon]$. Suppose a feasible filling $h$ satisfies $$\label{f:shell-room} \|h(x)-b(s)\|\le\operatorname{dist}(x,s)-2$$ for every movable endpoint $x$ of a tested central edge and every shell vertex $s$. If the edge is not fixed–fixed, there is a feasible filling whose absolute gradient on that edge is at most $1/2$.
  - Explanation: An interval extension construction relaxes a tested central edge when the shell has sufficient room and the interior prescriptions meet the stated bounds.
- **claim-conditioned-sparse-contacts** (bound, [source](#stmt-f-conditioned-sparse)): Fix a domain, fixed pin values in $[-1/2,1/2]$, and deterministic sign strings as described above, allowing additional intervals $[0,\varepsilon]$. For every prescribed animal parameter there are a fixed box size and $s>0$ such that, except on a bad set with that animal bound, the tested central edges involving nonfixed vertices have $\|\nabla h\|\le1-s$. String sites are included among the nonfixed vertices. Long-distance slack and this edge slack persist with relaxed constants during a sufficiently short stationary reflected step. Constants are uniform over the strings’ shape and over the positive interval lengths.
  - Explanation: Bounded fixed pins and movable sign intervals yield sparse near-contact edges, uniformly over string shape and positive interval lengths. Short stationary steps preserve relaxed slack.
- **claim-negative-sobolev-tightness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-f-tightness)): Suppose the rescaled free sets lie in a fixed bounded box, their exterior data are bounded, and a connected exterior pin set of macroscopic diameter is available in a fixed larger box. The centered fields, made constant on fundamental lattice cells of mesh $n^{-1}$ and extended by zero outside, are tight in $H^{-s}$ on a fixed surrounding torus for every $s>0$.
  - Explanation: Macroscopic moment bounds and cancellation of fine-scale wavelets give tightness of centered fields in negative Sobolev spaces.
- **claim-local-reflected-comparison** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-c-comparison)): Consider the experiments just specified, with $\|a\|+\|b\|$ bounded. Assume the conclusions of <a href="#f:conditioned-sparse" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:conditioned-sparse">12</a>, <a href="#f:hole" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:hole">6</a>, and <a href="#f:averages" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:averages">2</a> for their original marginal laws. Individual reflecting constraints are ordinary one-sided sign walls, not pairs $0\le h_x\le\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon$ allowed to tend to zero. Fix $0<r<R<2$, $1<p<2$, and a desired defect parameter $\rho>0$. There are fixed testing parameters, a step length $T_\rho>0$, good edges $G_n$ and good wall sites $S_n^{\rm g}$, and positive weights $w_e,w_x\le1$ with the following properties.* *For either tail in <a href="#c:tails" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="c:tails">[c:tails]</a>, or for their signed difference, let $$\label{c:energy} \mathcal E_n(Q)= \sum_{e\in G_n,\ e\subset Q}w_e\|\nabla_e u_0\|^2 +\sum_{x\in S_n^{\rm g}\cap Q}w_x\|u_0(x)\|^2.$$ In the two-tail statement the energies are added. In a free comparison the energy is that of $z$ and there is no wall sum. Then $$\label{c:energy-bound} \mathbb E\mathcal E_n(Q_r)\le C,\qquad \mathbb E\sum_{C:\,C\cap Q_r\ne\varnothing}D_C\le C.$$ Here $C$ and $D_C$ have the preceding step-cluster meaning. The constants in <a href="#c:energy-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="c:energy-bound">[c:energy-bound]</a> may depend on $\rho,p,r,R$ and the average bounds. Defective boxes satisfy the prescribed sparse-animal bound. For every fixed $q<\infty$ and $A<\infty$, the normalized spatial sums of $w^{-q}$, cluster-size moments, and hole-diameter moments are bounded by deterministic constants outside an event of probability $O(n^{-A})$. The relevant finite collection of moment orders can be chosen in advance.* *Let $U_n$ be the extension over holes supplied by <a href="#f:hole" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:hole">6</a>, with a fixed choice of the testing parameters. It can be set to zero on the exceptional event. In scaled coordinates, $$\label{c:compactness} \mathbb E\\|U_n\\|_{W^{1,p}(n^{-1}Q_r)}^2\le C,\qquad \mathbb E\int_{n,Q_r}\|U_n-u_0\|\longrightarrow0.$$ In a free comparison subtract a local cutoff-weighted average from both $U_n$ and $z_0$. Its gradient and dissipation estimates are unchanged. All these centered estimates are uniform in the size of the ambient domain. The same bounds hold for a rough one-sided adapted experiment with only $z\|_P\ge a$, for $u^-=(a-z)_+$, and with zero extension behind a controlled observed boundary. They hold uniformly after replacing $z$ by $z/K$, $K\ge1$, with bounded rescaled thresholds.* **Threshold-uniform specialization.* In the one-sided case, for each threshold $a$ satisfying the required condition $z\|_P\ge a$, the weights may be chosen independently of $a$. With the original marginal moment bounds fixed, $$\label{c:threshold-scaling} \mathbb E\mathcal E_n\bigl((a-z)_+;Q_r\bigr) +\mathbb E\\|U_n^{(a)}\\|_{W^{1,p}(n^{-1}Q_r)}^2 \le C_0(1+a^2).$$ Thus, when $a=K\ge1$ and the observed values satisfy $z\|_P\ge K$, the energy and squared Sobolev norm of $(1-z/K)_+$ are bounded by $2C_0$, uniformly in $K$.* *For an ordinary simply connected polygon domain with identical fixed boundary data, the exterior-preserving construction in Lemma <a href="#c:exterior-zero" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="c:exterior-zero">21</a> gives a bounded $W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^2)$ extension which is exactly zero outside the lattice polygon. This construction uses connectivity of its zero exterior; it is not asserted for an arbitrary disconnected internal observed set.* *If $Q_R$ has no observations or individual walls, and $X_n$ is sampled from normalized ambient volume in $Q_r$, then $n\nabla_{(X_n,X_n+\mathbf e)}z_0$ for each fixed lattice step $\mathbf e$, $n(z_0(X_n+i)-z_0(X_n))$ for each fixed lattice offset $i$, and $n\sup_{t\le T_0}\|z_t(X_n)-z_0(X_n)\|$ are tight. Thus this untruncated conclusion has a fixed positive macroscopic free buffer. It also holds up to controlled observations when $a=b$, because the two tails then control $z-a$. For general $a<b$, corresponding tightness statements hold only for the controlled tails up to observations. Here $T_0$ is one fixed sufficiently short step. Sampling is not conditioned on an arbitrarily small random free set.* *Finally these statements allow a drift difference bounded by $c n^{-2}$, with bounded support on the macroscopic scale, including a sufficiently small smooth exponential tilt of either marginal. Constants may depend on a fixed bound for $c$; the smallness needed for the change of marginal law is that in <a href="#f:averages" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:averages">2</a>.
  - Explanation: Stationary synchronous comparisons give weighted gradient and wall energies, dissipation bounds, filled Sobolev compactness, and microscopic tightness in the specified free or controlled-tail regimes. Adaptive observations are averaged over their actual transcripts.
- **claim-adapted-freezing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-c-freezing)): Conditional on an adapted exact-value transcript, the unqueried fields have the product of their Gibbs laws with those values pinned. Replacing this product by a stationary synchronous coupling preserves each annealed marginal and makes the coupled process stationary. The same marginal-preservation statement holds for jointly sampled boundary data with the conditional Gibbs kernels specified above.
  - Explanation: Adapted exact-value queries leave the product Gibbs kernel on unqueried coordinates. A stationary synchronous joining preserves each original annealed marginal.
- **claim-conditional-failure-control** (bound, [source](#stmt-c-conditional)): Let $A_i$ be future events and $\mathcal I$ the initial sigma-field. If every subset $J$ of a separated set satisfies $\mathbb P(\bigcap_{i\in J}A_i)\le\rho^{\|J\|}$, then, for $0<q<1$, $$\mathbb P\left(\bigcap_{i\in I} \{\mathbb P(A_i\mid\mathcal I)>q\}\right) \le \frac{2}{q}\bigl(2\rho^{q/2}\bigr)^{\|I\|}.$$ Also, if $0\le X_n\le n^B$ and $\mathbb P(X_n>M)\le n^{-A}$, then $$\mathbb P\{\mathbb E[X_n\mid\mathcal I]>M+1\}\le n^{B-A}.$$
  - Explanation: Joint sparse-event bounds control how often conditional failure probabilities are large. Polynomial exceptional bounds also transfer to conditional expectations after truncation.
- **claim-averaging-cluster-displacement** (bound, [source](#stmt-c-cluster)): On a zero-drift step, normal reflection of a difference acts on each transmission cluster by compositions of averaging projections and their convex mixtures. Free-input matrices are symmetric positive contractions at each projection, with nonnegative entries and row and column sums at most one. Pins supply their fixed difference; common individual walls supply zero. For a tail with zero pinned input, insert coordinate contractions after the averaging updates. If a cluster has $H$ free vertices and total square loss $D$, then $$\label{c:displacement} \sup_{t\le T}\max_{x\in C}\|u_t(x)-u_0(x)\| \le C(H+1)\sqrt D.$$ The same estimate holds for an untruncated conservative difference, and is invariant under addition of a constant.
  - Explanation: Normal reflection acts through averaging projections and contractions. Their square losses control displacement within a transmission cluster.
- **claim-facet-path-uniform-forcing** (construction, [source](#stmt-c-force)): Suppose every original edge involving a free coordinate has initial slack at least $s>0$. Assume that in both directed orientations every original-edge path between a central test vertex and the collar, without an individual-constraint edge to ground, has residual slack greater than $\Lambda>2$. Every free component is required to reach the collar or an observed fixed vertex through original edges. Ordinary sign walls are allowed, and a tested wall has initial slack at most one.* *For every central edge there are at most $N+1$ genuine facet constraints joining its endpoints, or grounding both endpoints at genuine pins or walls. A tested individual wall is grounded by such a path. For any fixed $T>0$ there are $p_0,I_0>0$, depending only on these fixed parameters, such that every facet selected in these paths can receive normal impulse at least $I_0$ in time $T$, on an event of the interior Brownian noises of probability at least $p_0$, while all collar coordinates move by less than $r_0$. Take $r_0<s/8$.
  - Explanation: Genuine facet paths replace possibly redundant tested constraints. Uniform interior slack and collar separation give a positive-probability Brownian forcing event with positive normal impulse.
- **claim-forcing-insulation** (bound, [source](#stmt-c-insulation)): Outside a sparse set of initially selected boxes, every interior forcing event in Lemma <a href="#c:force" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="c:force">19</a> has conditional probability at least $p_0/2$ of occurring in the uncut process, given the initial pair and transcript.
  - Explanation: Sparse conditional shell-displacement failures leave interior forcing events with a uniform positive probability in the original uncut process.
- **claim-connected-zero-exterior** (construction, [source](#stmt-c-exterior-zero)): Let $D_n$ be a finite simply connected triangular-lattice polygon. Let $E_n$ consist of its boundary vertices and all vertices outside its interior, and put $u=0$ on $E_n$. Assume $u$ is uniformly Lipschitz on the full lattice and has the good-edge energy and inverse-weight bounds established above, including edges incident to its fixed boundary. The hole extension can be chosen so that $U=0$ on $E_n$, with the same Sobolev estimate as in <a href="#f:hole" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:hole">6</a>. Its normalized annealed $L^1$ error tends to zero under the improved-parameter bounds used in <a href="#c:all-edge-l1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="c:all-edge-l1">[c:all-edge-l1]</a>. Thus the same-boundary comparison difference, extended by zero, has a filled extension satisfying $$\sup_n\mathbb E\\|U_n\\|_{W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^2)}^2<\infty,\qquad U_n=0\ \hbox{on }\mathbb R^2\setminus D_n$$ after scaling and affine interpolation, for every $1<p<2$.
  - Explanation: Connected exterior zero paths provide zero rim anchors for filled holes. This preserves the exact zero exterior and the global Sobolev estimate with vanishing filling error.
- **claim-stationary-bulk-environment** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-b-bulk)): Under the inputs specified above, the gradient process and its driving Brownian increments, viewed from a uniformly sampled vertex in a compact macroscopic region separated by a fixed positive macroscopic distance from all fixed pins and reflecting sign walls, have a unique local limit. This limit is independent of the bounded boundary data and of the small smooth tilts under consideration. It is stationary in space and time and spatially ergodic. Its local trajectories are continuous and have normal reflection. On a fixed short step, every vertex belongs to a finite transmission cluster; there are almost surely no simultaneous distinct-face contacts. A face visited away from the endpoints of a contact episode has positive reflection impulse in that episode.
  - Explanation: Bulk gradient trajectories and their Brownian drivers have a unique stationary, spatially ergodic local law independent of bounded boundary data and small smooth tilts. Isolated short-step clusters retain normal reflection and regular contacts.
- **claim-stable-tangent-product** (theorem, [source](#stmt-b-tangent)): On a finite isolated cluster, consider a normal-reflection trajectory with interior endpoints, no simultaneous distinct-face contacts, and positive impulse in each visited-face episode. For two compared trajectories whose initial states are sufficiently close to the reference initial state and which use the same driving path, sufficiently close to the reference drive, their synchronous difference update is exactly a finite product $$J=P_{e_k}\cdots P_{e_1}.$$ Consequently, if the initial relative differences multiplied by $n$ are tight, their limiting update is $w'=Jw$ modulo constants. An additional relative drift bounded by $Cn^{-2}$ makes a vanishing error after this multiplication by $n$.
  - Explanation: Regular isolated reflection trajectories have an exact finite projection-product update for close synchronous differences. This exact identity survives the scaled tangent limit.
- **claim-volume-sampled-tangent-extraction** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-b-extraction)): Let $z$ be a stationary comparison on scale $n$ covered by Theorem <a href="#c:comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="c:comparison">15</a>, with relative drift $n^{-2}b(x/n)$. Sample $x$ in a fixed compact macroscopic region separated by a positive macroscopic distance from all fixed pins and reflecting sign walls. Extract local limits of $n(z_{x+i}-z_x)$, jointly with $x/n$ and the bulk environment. Conditional on the macroscopic position, the limit is a stationary spatial cocycle, has update $w'=Jw$ modulo constants, and has affine volume growth with a possibly random slope $q$. Conditional on almost every value of $q$, it is a controlled solution on the original environment law. If the expected macroscopic difference converges to $m$, then $$\mathbb E[q\mid x/n=y]=\nabla m(y)$$ in the distributional sense in the interior.
  - Explanation: Volume sampling extracts stationary tangent cocycles with affine volume growth. Conditioning on almost every attained slope preserves the bulk environment, and expected slopes identify the macroscopic mean gradient.
- **claim-forward-contact-recurrence** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-b-recurrence)): Fix an edge. Suppose that there are forward-past measurable events $G_j$ with $\mathbb P(G_j)\to1$. For each $j$, suppose a finite measurable cover of $G_j$ assigns to each class a fixed finite path of genuine free facets connecting the edge endpoints. Assume each assigned facet can be forced during a bounded time interval with conditional probability at least $p_j>0$, given the entire forward history at the start of that interval. Then the future contact graph connects the edge endpoints almost surely. If these assumptions hold for every lattice edge, that graph is connected.
  - Explanation: High-probability forward-past opportunity classes and uniformly positive facet forcing connect the future contact graph without requiring temporal ergodicity.
- **claim-force-opportunity-transfer** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-b-force-transfer)): The finite-cover force and insulation estimates of Lemmas <a href="#c:force" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="c:force">19</a> and <a href="#c:insulation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="c:insulation">20</a>, with the improving good-configuration probabilities in <a href="#f:conditioned-sparse" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:conditioned-sparse">12</a> and <a href="#c:short-step" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="c:short-step">[c:short-step]</a>, imply the hypotheses of Lemma <a href="#b:recurrence" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="b:recurrence">27</a> for the bulk environment.
  - Explanation: Finite-volume force inequalities pass to the full unmarked forward filtration. Conditional opportunity classes then provide the contact-recurrence hypotheses.
- **claim-zero-slope-uniqueness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-b-zero-slope)): A controlled tangent solution of slope zero is spatially constant.
  - Explanation: Stationarity, sublinear volume growth, and integrable dissipation force every zero-slope controlled tangent field to be spatially constant.
- **claim-cell-flux-weak-equation** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-b-cell)): Under the preceding inputs, $j(q)$ is well defined on the vector space of attained slopes and is linear there. If any nonzero slope is attained, every slope in $\mathbb R^2$ is attained and $j(q)=Aq$ for a finite scalar $A$. For a stationary comparison with drift difference $n^{-2}b(x/n)$, every subsequential expected macroscopic difference $m$ satisfies $$\label{b:weak-equation} \int j(\nabla m)\cdot\nabla f=\int b f, \qquad f\in C_c^\infty(U),$$ in each limiting open region $U$ free of observations.
  - Explanation: Controlled solutions have a unique linear mean flux on attained slopes. Lattice symmetries make the flux scalar once a nonzero slope is attained, and stationarity yields the interior weak response equation.
- **claim-positive-dirichlet-response** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-b-response)): Assume the comparison and average estimates hold up to identical fixed boundaries of lattice domains converging to a bounded smooth domain $D$. Then every slope is attained and the scalar in Proposition <a href="#b:cell" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="b:cell">30</a> satisfies $0<A<\infty$. For sufficiently small smooth sources $b$, the mean response to relative drift $n^{-2}b(x/n)$ converges to $$A^{-1}(-\Delta_D)^{-1}b.$$ For boundary values $+\lambda$ and $-\lambda$ on the two marked arcs, the untilted mean converges to their bounded harmonic extension.
  - Explanation: A positive source excludes a trivial attained-slope space and identifies a finite positive stiffness coefficient. Zero-exterior comparison fixes the Dirichlet response, while boundary comparisons identify the harmonic mean.
- **claim-dirichlet-field-limit** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-b-gff)): Under the inputs of this section for the ordinary fixed-boundary domains, the centered affinely interpolated field converges as a random distribution to $\sigma$ times the Dirichlet Gaussian free field with covariance $(-\Delta_D)^{-1}$, where $$\sigma^2=(vA)^{-1}.$$ The stiffness is $vA$, and the limiting mean is the harmonic extension identified in Proposition <a href="#b:response" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="b:response">31</a>.
  - Explanation: Differentiating small-tilt moment generating functions identifies Gaussian finite-dimensional laws. Distributional tightness and interpolation estimates give the centered affine field limit.
- **claim-quantitative-frostman-traces** (bound, [source](#stmt-t-frostman)): Let $1<p<2$, $0<\alpha\le1$, and $p+\alpha>2$. Every $u\in W^{1,p}(Q^*)$ has a trace $T_\mu u\in L^1(\mu)$ for $\mu\in\mathcal M_\alpha(M)$, and $$\label{t:trace-rate} \int\|T_\mu u-P_ru\|\,\mathrm d\mu \le C r^\beta\\|\nabla u\\|_{L^p(Q^*)},\qquad \beta=1-\frac{2-\alpha}{p}>0.$$ The constant is uniform over $\mathcal M_\alpha(M)$.* *For a piecewise affine mesh function $u_n$, suppose instead that a measure on mesh vertices satisfies $$\label{t:coarse-frostman} \mu_n(B(x,r))\le C(r+\ell_n/n)^\alpha, \qquad \mu_n(\overline Q)\le C,$$ where $1\le\ell_n\le C(\log n)^C$. Then, for fixed $r>0$, $$\label{t:mesh-trace-rate} \int\|u_n-P_ru_n\|\,\mathrm d\mu_n \le C\left(r^\beta+ \ell_n^{\alpha/p}n^{-\beta}\right) \\|\nabla u_n\\|_{L^p(Q^*)}.$$
  - Explanation: Dyadic averaging constructs traces against Frostman measures and gives a quantitative averaging error. Mesh measures require an additional bottom-scale term.
- **claim-frostman-measure-transport** (construction, [source](#stmt-t-transport)): Suppose $K$ has continuum thickness below $r_0$. If $\mu\in\mathcal M_\alpha(M)$ is supported within distance $\eta$ of $K$, where $0<\eta<r_0/10$, there is a measure $\nu\in\mathcal M_\alpha(CM)$ supported on $K$ and a coupling $\pi$ of $\mu,\nu$ supported on $\|x-y\|\le C\eta$. Consequently $$\label{t:transport-trace} \int\|T_\mu u(x)-T_\nu u(y)\|\,\mathrm d\pi(x,y) \le C\eta^\beta\\|\nabla u\\|_p$$ under the exponent assumptions of Lemma <a href="#t:frostman" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="t:frostman">35</a>.* *If mesh sets $K_n$ have the common thickness constants and converge to $K$ in Hausdorff distance, every such measure supported on $K$ is the weak limit of continuous measures in $\mathcal M_\alpha(CM)$ supported on $K_n$. For geometric mesh graphs, these may additionally be projected onto their vertices, giving the common bound $C(r+n^{-1})^\alpha$.
  - Explanation: Thickness supplies nearby continua onto which testing mass can be transported while preserving ball-mass bounds. The same construction approximates testing measures on varying mesh sets.
- **claim-weighted-anchor-errors** (bound, [source](#stmt-t-anchors)): Let $q>1$, and let $S_n$ be retained observed vertices with positive weights $w_x$. Suppose $$\sum_{x\in S_n}w_x\|z_x\|^2\le E_n, \qquad n^{-2}\sum_{x\in S_n}w_x^{-q}\le C_q.$$ For a probability measure $\mu_n$ on these vertices with $a_n=\max_x\mu_n(\{x\})$, $$\label{t:anchor-rate} \sum_x\mu_n(\{x\})\|z_x\| \le C_q E_n^{1/2}n^{1/q}a_n^{(1+1/q)/2}.$$ In particular, if $a_n\le C(\ell_n/n)^\alpha$, the bound tends to zero in expectation when $\sup_n\mathbb EE_n<\infty$ and $q>(2-\alpha)/\alpha$. The deterministic inverse-weight bound may hold outside exceptional events, provided their contributions to the displayed quantities tend to zero.
  - Explanation: Anchor energy and deterministic inverse-weight moments control testing-measure errors. A sufficiently large reciprocal-weight moment makes these errors vanish.
- **claim-varying-observed-zero-trace** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-t-varying-trace)): Let $K_n$ have the mesh thickness property with common constants and converge in Hausdorff distance to $K$. Let their mesh vertices carry random values $z_n$, and let $U_n$ be random piecewise affine extensions on $Q^*$. Fix $3/2<p<2$. Assume the following bounds, uniformly in $n$:* 1. *$\mathbb E\\|U_n\\|_{W^{1,p}}\le C$, and the means $\mathbb EU_n$ have a subsequence converging strongly in $L^p$ to $u$;* 2. *every vertex on $K_n$ can be moved to a retained vertex on $K_n$ within distance $\ell_n/n$, where $\ell_n\le C(\log n)^C$;* 3. *$U_n=z_n$ at retained vertices, and their values satisfy Lemma <a href="#t:anchors" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="t:anchors">37</a> for some $q>3$, with $\mathbb EE_n\le C$;* 4. *exceptional events in these assertions have vanishing contribution to the Sobolev, anchor, and fixed-scale averaged quantities used here.* *Then $u$ has zero $1/2$-Frostman trace on $K$ and is zero Lebesgue-almost everywhere on $K$. If the original interpolated values also satisfy $$\label{t:original-filled} \mathbb E\\|z_n-U_n\\|_{L^1(Q)}\longrightarrow0,$$ then the original mean responses have the same distributional limit, including for smooth tests whose supports meet $K$.
  - Explanation: Strong convergence of mean filled extensions, retained-site transport, and anchor control give zero Frostman trace and vanishing almost everywhere on the limiting observed set. Vanishing original–filled error transfers the same limit to the original means.
- **claim-brownian-approach-measures** (bound, [source](#stmt-t-exit)): Let $K$ have continuum thickness, put $V=Q\setminus K$, and fix $z\in V$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, let $V_\varepsilon$ be the component containing $z$ of $\{x\in V:\operatorname{dist}(x,V^c)>\varepsilon\}$. The exit law $\mu_{z,\varepsilon}$ of Brownian motion from $V_\varepsilon$ satisfies $$\label{t:exit-frostman} \mu_{z,\varepsilon}(B(x,r))\le C_z r^{1/2},$$ uniformly in $\varepsilon$. The constant is uniform for $z$ a positive distance from $K$, and depends on the common thickness constants and $Q$.
  - Explanation: Thickness and the inward Beurling estimate give uniform Frostman bounds for Brownian exit measures from interior approximations.
- **claim-poisson-uniqueness-frostman-trace** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-trace)): Let $K\subset\overline Q$ contain $\partial Q$ and have continuum thickness below $r_0$. Let $3/2<p<2$, $A>0$, and $b\in L^\infty(Q)$. Suppose $u\in W^{1,p}(Q^*)$ has zero $1/2$-Frostman trace on $K$ and $$-A\Delta u=b\quad\hbox{in }V=Q\setminus K$$ in the sense of distributions. Then, on $Q$, $$\label{t:poisson-identification} u=A^{-1}G_Vb,$$ where the right side is extended by zero on $K$. In particular the restriction of $u$ to $V$ belongs to $H^1_0(V)$.
  - Explanation: Zero Frostman trace and the distributional Poisson equation identify the solution with the variational Dirichlet Green solution, including its zero values on positive-area parts of the observed set.
- **claim-deterministic-string-covariance** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-t-covariance)): Suppose the class $\mathcal S_n$ and the estimates <a href="#t:input-moments" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="t:input-moments">[t:input-moments]</a>–<a href="#t:input-flux" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="t:input-flux">[t:input-flux]</a> hold, and set $\sigma^2=(vA)^{-1}$. Along every deterministic sequence $s_n\in\mathcal S_n$ with $K_{n,s_n}\to K$ in Hausdorff distance, $$\label{t:conditional-mgf} \log\mathbb E_{n,s_n}e^{tX_{n,s_n}(f)} \longrightarrow \frac{t^2\sigma^2}{2}\langle f,G_{Q\setminus K}f\rangle$$ for $t$ in a neighborhood of zero. The conclusion holds for convergent sequences of tests from a compact family and jointly for finitely many tests. In particular, $$\label{t:uniform-covariance} \sup_{s\in\mathcal S_n}\sup_{f,g\in\mathcal C} \left\|\operatorname{Cov}_{n,s}(X_{n,s}(f),X_{n,s}(g)) -\sigma^2\langle f,G_{V_{n,s}}g\rangle\right\| \longrightarrow0.$$ There is no requirement that $K$ have zero area or that the test supports be disjoint from $K$.
  - Explanation: Uniform moments, filled response traces, and the bulk equation identify Gaussian conditional pairings and uniformly convergent Dirichlet covariances for deterministic sign strings.
- **claim-thick-set-green-continuity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-green-continuity)): If compact sets $K_n$ containing $\partial Q$ satisfy the common thickness condition and tend in Hausdorff distance to $K$, then $$\langle f_n,G_{Q\setminus K_n}g_n\rangle \longrightarrow\langle f,G_{Q\setminus K}g\rangle$$ whenever bounded smooth tests $f_n,g_n$ converge uniformly to $f,g$. The same assertion holds for mesh-thick approximants.
  - Explanation: Common thickness lets zero traces pass through Hausdorff limits, identifying the limit of variational Green solutions and their pairings.
- **claim-random-string-kernel-transfer** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-t-random-covariance)): Let $S_n$ take values in $\mathcal S_n$, and suppose $$\label{t:kernel} \operatorname{Law}(h_n\mid S_n=s)=P_{n,s} \quad\hbox{for almost every }s.$$ Then, for fixed tests or compact families as in Theorem <a href="#t:covariance" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="t:covariance">42</a>, the conditional covariance differs in $L^1$ from $\sigma^2\langle f,G_{V_{n,S_n}}g\rangle$ by $o(1)$. If $K_{n,S_n}$ converges in distribution to $K$, these random Green forms converge in distribution and in expectation to those on $Q\setminus K$. Convergence in $L^1$ to a limiting random form additionally requires that the sets converge in probability on a common probability space.
  - Explanation: An exact conditional Gibbs kernel transfers deterministic uniform covariance estimates to random strings. Convergence in probability on a common space is additionally needed for convergence in mean to a limiting random form.
- **claim-near-continuum-variance-vanishing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-t-boundary-variance)): Let $K$ satisfy Definition <a href="#t:thickness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="t:thickness">33</a> and let $V=Q\setminus K$. Let $\mu_\varepsilon$ be positive measures of mass at most one, supported in $V$ within distance $C\varepsilon$ of $K$, with a common $1/2$-Frostman constant. Then $$\label{t:boundary-energy} \langle\mu_\varepsilon,G_V\mu_\varepsilon\rangle\longrightarrow0.$$ The conclusion holds for any unnormalized restriction of such a measure. It holds uniformly after adding further observed sets: if $K'\supset K$ and $V'=Q\setminus K'$, the Green quadratic form on $V'$ is bounded above by that on $V$.
  - Explanation: Frostman control handles the Green singularity, while Beurling control suppresses transport away from the nearby continuum. Further observations can only decrease the Green quadratic form.
- **claim-ambient-uniform-local-boundary-variance** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-t-local-boundary-variance)): Fix nested squares $Q_0\Subset Q_1\Subset Q_2\Subset Q_3$ and positive geometric separation constants. Consider finite triangular-lattice domains of mesh $n^{-1}$, with arbitrary ambient diameter, fixed data in $[-1/2,1/2]$, and deterministic sign strings. Suppose a connected observed piece of diameter at least $c>0$ lies within bounded distance of $Q_2$. Assume the local hypotheses of <a href="#f:averages" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:averages">2</a> and <a href="#c:comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="c:comparison">15</a>, with constants independent of ambient diameter. Assume also that restricting the observed system to $Q_3$ and adjoining its artificial exterior gives the common mesh thickness constants of Definition <a href="#t:thickness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="t:thickness">33</a>. This holds for connected strands attached to the original exterior, or for components of uniformly positive diameter: cut pieces meeting the artificial boundary join that boundary, and pieces entirely inside are whole original components.* *For each fixed $\eta>0$, let $\mu_{n,\eta}$ be a deterministic smooth probability test supported in $Q_0$, at distance at most $C\eta$ from the observed set in $Q_1$. Suppose these measures have a common $1/2$-Frostman constant, independent of $n,\eta$, and for fixed $\eta$ their densities range over a compact smooth-test family. If $X_n(\mu)$ denotes the Riemann pairing of the centered field with that density, then $$\label{t:local-variance-limit} \lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\limsup_{n\to\infty} \sup\operatorname{Var}X_n(\mu_{n,\eta})=0.$$ The supremum is over the stated local geometries, tests, and arbitrary ambient domains. The inner limit is always taken at fixed $\eta$.
  - Explanation: A bounded auxiliary domain and local comparison transfer boundary variance decay to domains of arbitrary ambient size. The mesh limit precedes shrinking the approach scale.
- **claim-tangential-divergence-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-shift-divergence)): Let $P\subset\mathbb R^N$ be a compact full-dimensional polytope, with normalized Lebesgue measure. Suppose that $u:P\to\mathbb R^N$ is Lipschitz and tangent to each facet of $P$. Then $$\label{eq:shift-divergence} \mathbb E\operatorname{div}u=0,\qquad \mathbb E(\operatorname{div}u)^2 =\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}\bigl((Du)^2\bigr) \leq\mathbb E\\|Du\\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2.$$
  - Explanation: Small positive and negative tangential perturbations preserve the polytope. Comparing determinant coefficients gives the divergence identities and the Hilbert–Schmidt bound.
- **claim-feasible-volume-controlled-shifts** (construction, [source](#stmt-g-shifts)): Under the sparse-box estimates <a href="#f:sparse" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:sparse">4</a> and <a href="#f:conditioned-sparse" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="f:conditioned-sparse">12</a> in the applicable conditioning class, let $f_n$ satisfy <a href="#eq:shift-prescription" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:shift-prescription">[eq:shift-prescription]</a>. For each $p_0>0$ there are $c>0$ and $n_0$, uniform over the allowed conditioning systems, with the following property. For $n\geq n_0$ and every measurable event $E$ with $\mathbb P(E)\geq p_0$, there is a measurable $E'\subset E$ with $\mathbb P(E')\geq p_0/2$ such that $T(h)=h+u(h)$ is injective on $E'$, has feasible image, and $$\sup_{h\in E'}\\|T(h)-h-f_n\\|_\infty=o(1),\qquad \mathbb P(T(E'))\geq c.$$ The statement also holds for a fixed finite product of independent conditional surfaces.
  - Explanation: Threshold-averaged component shifts approximate a slowly varying prescription, preserve hard constraints, and retain positive image probability on a large subevent through injectivity and determinant control.
- **claim-bounded-local-sign-insertion** (construction, [source](#stmt-g-insertion)): For every fixed $L<\infty$ there is $p_L>0$ with the following property. Condition on any admissible exact oriented strands. In a patch of diameter at most $L$, at distance at most $L$ from one of their tips or from bounded Dirichlet boundary, prescribe a compatible sign pattern on at most $L$ additional vertices. The probability of that pattern is at least $p_L$. In particular every feasible prescribed extension of at most $L$ interface steps has a probability bounded below by a constant depending only on $L$. There are also absolute $p_*,b_*>0$ such that every nonfixed positive string site has conditional probability at least $p_*$ to have height greater than $b_*$, without any restriction on its distance from strand tips or Dirichlet boundary. Both assertions remain valid when other positive string sites have additional upper bounds in $(0,d]$, provided neither a prescribed new positive site nor the tested string site is one of those upper-bounded sites.
  - Explanation: Good shells and contraction toward a compatible strict filling give a uniform lower probability for bounded local sign insertions. A separate singleton assertion controls positive string heights away from tips.
- **claim-screened-controlled-pin-comparison** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-g-screened-comparison)): Consider a one-sided experiment from Theorem <a href="#c:comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="c:comparison">15</a> at scale $R\to\infty$, after an adapted exact-value transcript has been recorded. Let $G$ be a recorded union of components of the common unqueried graph. Every original lattice edge from $G$ to its complement must end at a common fixed vertex; no free–free edge is deleted in selecting $G$. There are no unrecorded individual walls in $G$. Write $P$ for all fixed vertices incident to $G$, $z=h-\widetilde h$, and consider either $$u=(a-z)_+,\quad P_{\rm c}=\{p\in P:z(p)\ge a\}, \qquad\hbox{or}\qquad u=(z-b)_+,\quad P_{\rm c}=\{p\in P:z(p)\le b\},$$ with bounded threshold. Put $P_{\rm u}=P\setminus P_{\rm c}$ and define $$\delta_G(x,P_{\rm u})= \inf\{\operatorname{diam}_\infty\gamma: \gamma=(x,\ldots,p)\text{ is a lattice path with } \gamma\setminus\{p\}\subset G,\ p\in P_{\rm u}\}. \tag{SC1}$$ Fixed vertices are terminal, not traversable, in (SC1), and an empty infimum is infinity.* *Let $Q_{\rm in}\Subset Q_{\rm out}$ be coordinate squares fixed before the transcript is sampled, with separation comparable to $R$ and $\operatorname{diam}_\infty Q_{\rm out}\le(c_0-c_1)R$ for a fixed $c_1>0$. Suppose that a tested set $T\subset G\cap Q_{\rm in}$ satisfies $\delta_G(x,P_{\rm u})\ge c_0R$ for every $x\in T$. Assume the original annealed sparse-contact, hole, and deterministic-test average hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#c:comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="c:comparison">15</a> in a fixed enlargement of $Q_{\rm out}$. Use full ambient Lipschitz extensions of both marginals. In particular the negative Sobolev bound is for the full, unmasked $z$ there, including its zeroth-scale anchored average. Then the one-sided conclusions of that theorem hold on $Q_{\rm in}$ for the components meeting $T$, with the tail extended by zero behind their controlled fixed boundary. Its hole extension $U$ satisfies, for every $1<p<2$, $$\mathbb E\\|U\\|_{W^{1,p}(R^{-1}Q_{\rm in})}^2\le C,\qquad \mathbb ER^{-2}\sum_{x\in T}\|U(x)-u(x)\|\longrightarrow0. \tag{SC2}$$ It is zero at retained vertices of $P_{\rm c}$ in this window. The constants may depend on the square ratios and $c_0$. The same statement holds on a recorded event of probability at least $p_*>0$, with constants depending on $p_*$. No estimate is asserted at a test with short access to $P_{\rm u}$. A trace application must separately verify thickness and transport to retained controlled pins; the artificial rim is not a zero-tail trace anchor.
  - Explanation: One-sided comparison remains valid on recorded free components whose tests have a macroscopic access-diameter margin from uncontrolled terminal pins. The full ambient field supplies the negative Sobolev bound.
- **claim-positive-pure-side-trace** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-sign-trace)): In a local sector with only positive string boundary, the limiting bounded harmonic conditional mean has Brownian boundary trace at least $c>0$, away from endpoints and incompatible sides. Here a testing neighborhood has a fixed access-diameter margin, in the actual free graph after the string heights are frozen, from every incident boundary pin not controlled by the comparison below; fixed pins cannot be traversed. On a negative sector its trace is at most $-c$. On an exterior boundary arc alone the trace is its prescribed value. If the pure sector also has positive exterior pins at least $\lambda_*>0$, its lower bound is $c\wedge\lambda_*$; the negative mixed sector is reflected. These statements are sequentially uniform at diverging lattice scales.
  - Explanation: Insertion and monotone comparison with fair bounded pins give a strictly signed boundary trace on screened pure sectors. Exterior-only sectors retain their prescribed boundary value.
- **claim-complete-crosscut-mean-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-upper-half)): For a complete single crosscut, the positive-side conditional mean is at most $1/2$, and the negative-side conditional mean is at least $-1/2$. This assertion is not made at an open interface tip.
  - Explanation: Deleting crossing constraints after completing the crosscut permits a reflection-symmetric comparison law that bounds the side means. The bound is not asserted at an open tip.
- **claim-high-corridor-crossing-decay** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-high-crossing)): In a compact corridor of fixed shape and size $n$, with an observed component of comparable size and distance, the probability of a path of heights at least $K$ crossing a fixed positive fraction of that corridor tends to zero as $K\to\infty$, after $n\to\infty$. The same is true for the difference of two independent samples under possibly different bounded exterior or strand conditionings. In both statements the corridor has an enlarged neighborhood of width $cn$, for a fixed $c>0$, containing no original fixed pins or sign walls. In the two-field statement this neighborhood lies in both domains with the same unconditioned lattice graph, and each original law has the stated macroscopic anchor. The two conditionings may differ outside this neighborhood.
  - Explanation: A hypothetical persistent high crossing would force a normalized tail to be positive in the bulk and have zero trace on a macroscopic continuum, contradicting the trace estimates.
- **claim-straight-layout-barrier-avoidance** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-g-barriers)): Fix $\theta>0,m<\infty,a>0$, and for mixed layouts fix $\kappa>0$. There is $p>0$ such that, for every compatible collection of at most $m$ $(\theta,R)$-barriers with the preceding layout, the conditional probability that all continuations of the observed strands avoid all the barriers is at least $p$. Pure exterior attachments are allowed when the prescribed heights are at least $\lambda_*>0$ on a positive attachment and at most $-\lambda_*$ on a negative attachment; $p$ may then depend on $\lambda_*$. Interior attachment constants do not depend on it.* *For diverging-scale applications assume local thickness in the endpoint testing windows: after cutting the observed system by a generous square of side comparable to $d$, each retained component meets its rim or has diameter at least $cd$, and a nearby attachment component has diameter at least $cd$. At bounded lattice scales the compatible finite sign fences are required not to prescribe both signs on one hexagon; they are treated by insertion.
  - Explanation: Screened attachments, local variance decay, high-crossing control, and feasible shifts build strict sign fences. They give uniform barrier avoidance for the stated straight-attachment layouts.
- **claim-exact-strand-law-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-strand-comparison)): Fix concentric inner and outer disks with radii in a fixed ratio strictly greater than one. Consider two base conditioning systems whose domains contain the closed outer disk and have the same unconditioned lattice graph there. All vertices constrained by the original strand observations, additional walls, or Dirichlet data must be outside the outer disk in both systems. Thus the entire outer disk, not just its annulus, is free in the two base laws. Each system has anchored observed or Dirichlet pieces of comparable diameter and distance outside this disk. Let $I$ specify a bounded collection of oriented strands all of whose adjacent sign-constrained vertices lie in the inner disk. Then $$C^{-1}\mathbb P_2(I)\leq\mathbb P_1(I)\leq C\mathbb P_2(I),$$ with a constant depending only on the fixed ratios and number of strands. The graphs need agree only inside the outer disk. The assertion does not compare laws with different pre-existing inner observations.
  - Explanation: Opposite-order circuits in a completely free buffer isolate dependency components. A measure-preserving replica swap transfers the inner strand event between the two base laws.
- **claim-logarithmic-hookup-probability** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-hookup)): For $9R/8<R'<5R$, with the observer and exterior boundary outside $\mathfrak B_{6R}$, there is a universal upper bound for all $R\geq R_0$, where $R_0>1$ is fixed: $$\mathbb P(Z^\sigma\mid\Phi_{R'},\Theta_R)\leq C/\log R. \tag{G1}$$ For every $a>0$ there is $c(a)>0$ such that the same probability is at least $c(a)/\log R$ when $Q(\Phi_{R'})\wedge Q(\Theta_R)\geq a$ and $R\geq R_0(a)$.
  - Explanation: Separated field corridors and a walk point-hitting estimate give a logarithmic lower bound for hookup. The matching upper bound remains available with the middle walk bridge unexposed.
- **claim-harmonic-landing-separation** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-separation)): For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $c(\varepsilon)>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $R$, $$\mathbb P\bigl(Q(\Phi_{3R})\wedge Q(\Theta_{2R})>c(\varepsilon) \mid\Phi_{4R},\Theta_R,Z^\sigma\bigr)>1-\varepsilon. \tag{G2}$$ The estimate is uniform in admissible records for which the conditioning has positive probability. The observer and original boundary are outside $\mathfrak B_{12R}$.
  - Explanation: Direct steering, positive completion support, and growth–collapse rounds improve the smaller physical separation. Hookup normalization then yields high-probability quality at the intermediate records.
- **claim-sampled-configuration-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-sample-comparison)): There are $C<\infty$ and $R_0<\infty$ such that the following holds for $R\geq R_0$. Take two domains containing $\mathfrak B_{12R}$, with observers outside that disk, and any two external records $\phi,\phi'$ at radius $4R$ having positive hookup probability. For every event $H$ determined by the initially unoriented $\Theta_R$, with the same specified geometric incident-edge label in the two experiments and no conditioning on the landing side, $$C^{-1}\mathbb P'(H\mid\Phi'_{4R}=\phi',Z'^\sigma) \leq \mathbb P(H\mid\Phi_{4R}=\phi,Z^\sigma) \leq C\mathbb P'(H\mid\Phi'_{4R}=\phi',Z'^\sigma). \tag{G7}$$ The constant is independent of $R$ and of additional unused annuli outside radius $4R$.
  - Explanation: Separation and logarithmic hookup estimates normalize comparable inner field and walk records. The comparison applies to unoriented geometric records with the landing side averaged.
- **claim-no-additional-sampled-excursions** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-extra)): Let $\mathcal J(r,R)$ be the event that more than two disjoint interface arcs cross from $\mathfrak B_r$ to $\partial\mathfrak B_R$, or that the walk exits $\mathfrak B_R$ after first entering $\mathfrak B_r$ and before its landing at zero. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are $A(\varepsilon)<\infty$ and $r_0(\varepsilon)<\infty$ such that $$\mathbb P(\mathcal J(r,R)\mid\Phi_R,\Theta_r,Z^\sigma)<\varepsilon \tag{G8}$$ when $r\geq r_0(\varepsilon)$, $R>A(\varepsilon)r$, the observer and boundary are outside $\mathfrak B_{4R}$, and the conditioning has positive probability. The same holds, with a harmless change of $\varepsilon$, conditioned only on $\Phi_R$ and $Z=\{S_\tau=0\}$.
  - Explanation: Separated records, confined walk bridges, and repeated single-sign barriers exclude additional annular interface crossings and large post-entry walk excursions under harmonic landing.
- **claim-original-boundary-landing-clearance** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-boundary-landing)): Let $S$ be an independent full walk from $v$, stopped only on the original boundary at $\tau_D$, and let $\gamma$ be the completed interface. Put $d=\operatorname{dist}(v,\partial D)$ and $$M=\{S_j:j<\tau_D,\ S_j\text{ is adjacent to }\gamma\}.$$ Under $(\mathrm{GB})$, uniformly over domains, observers, and the indicated exterior data, $$\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\limsup_{d\to\infty} \mathbb P\bigl(\operatorname{dist}(M,\partial D)<\eta d\bigr)=0. \tag{GB1}$$ The distance of the empty set is infinity. In particular the assertion holds for a terminal harmonic landing, or simultaneously for every old-prefix landing of this walk that is not on $\partial D$.
  - Explanation: Pure-arc repulsion and an independent full-walk exit comparison keep interface-adjacent walk vertices away from the original boundary in the iterated limit. The estimate covers all prefix landings pathwise.
- **claim-observer-interface-clearance** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-observer-landing)): Uniformly over the same bounded-data experiments, $$\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\limsup_{d\to\infty} \mathbb P\{\operatorname{dist}(v,\gamma)<\eta d\}=0. \tag{GB4}$$ This assertion does not require the lower bound in $(\mathrm{GB})$.
  - Explanation: Nested free sign shields keep the interface from approaching a fixed interior observer. This estimate does not need the exterior positive lower bound.
- **claim-stopped-harmonic-landing-survival** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-survival)): Let $T$ be any stopping time for the filtration generated by oriented initial interface pieces, $K=\gamma[0,T]$, and $d=\operatorname{dist}(v,\partial D)$. Let $X_T$ be the first landing of an independent full walk $S$ on $\partial D(K)$; let $Y$ be its landing for the completed interface. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are $p>0$, $d_0<\infty$ such that $$\mathbb P\bigl(\mathbb P(Y=X_T\mid K,S)<p\bigr)<\varepsilon \qquad(d>d_0), \tag{G9}$$ uniformly over the domains, observers, and stopping times under $(\mathrm{GB})$.
  - Explanation: A compatible barrier protects the previously sampled walk from later interface growth. Except on a small event, the conditional probability that the old landing survives is bounded below.
- **claim-stopped-harmonic-landing-nonreturn** (bound, [source](#stmt-g-nonreturn)): For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are $s>0$ and $d_0<\infty$ such that $$\mathbb P\bigl(d(X_T,\gamma\setminus\gamma[0,T])<s d,\, X_T\notin\partial D\bigr)<\varepsilon \qquad(d>d_0), \tag{G11}$$ uniformly over all sign-filtration stopping times $T$, with $d=\operatorname{dist}(v,\partial D)$, under $(\mathrm{GB})$.
  - Explanation: Survival reweighting transfers completed sampled-excursion bounds to stopped landings. Separate shields in the relevant accesses then exclude future Euclidean return.
- **claim-labelled-physical-slit-sampling** (construction, [source](#stmt-h-slit-sampling)): Let the original Jordan lattice domains be contained in one fixed bounded set. Let $U_n$ be the component containing an observer $z_n$ after removing a simple dual prefix, or after cutting along a complete simple dual crosscut. Suppose $\operatorname{dist}(z_n,\partial U_n)\ge\rho>0$ in physical units. Label its prime-end boundary by the original positive and negative arcs and the two oriented strand sides; empty arcs are allowed. There are at most four cyclic arcs before completion and at most two in a completed component.* *Kill triangular-lattice walk on its first visit to the original boundary or to a vertex adjacent to the explored strand. Original boundary values take priority at a vertex of both types. Let $\xi_n$ denote this landing with its incident-side label. There is a coupling with Brownian exit $\xi_n^{\rm B}$ from $U_n$ such that, for every $a>0$, $$\sup_{U_n,z_n} \mathbb P\{\|\xi_n-\xi_n^{\rm B}\|>a \text{ or their labels differ}\}\longrightarrow0 . \tag{H2}$$ The supremum includes all such prefixes, hence all stopping rules. Repeated Euclidean boundary points are distinguished by their incident accesses.
  - Explanation: A domain-independent walk–Brownian coupling and mixed-access screening match both exit locations and incident-side labels uniformly over protected physical slits.
- **claim-marked-domain-harmonic-limits** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h-marked-limits)): In the setting of Lemma <a href="#h:slit-sampling" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="h:slit-sampling">66</a>, let the observers converge, $z_n\to z$, and take a Hausdorff subsequence of the closed removed sets consisting of the explored slit and the original exterior. Retain the conformal maps from the disk to the observer components, normalized by $f_n(0)=z_n$ and $f_n'(0)>0$, and the inverse images of all boundary-label transition accesses. After a further subsequence on which these marks converge, bounded harmonic functions with the prescribed finite label values converge on compact subsets to the Poisson extension of the limiting marked arc data. Their harmonic boundary samples converge with these marks. At a surviving common local boundary piece of two such domains, the limit preserves the incident-side identification.
  - Explanation: Retaining normalized conformal maps and boundary transition accesses makes labelled Poisson extensions and harmonic samples converge without reconstructing side labels from closed sets alone.
- **claim-common-lower-reading-kernel** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h-common-kernel)): For $1\le i\le k$, let $U^i_n,V^i_n$ take values in $[-M,M]$, with $U^i_n$ measurable with respect to a sigma-field $\mathcal A^i_n$. Suppose that $$\mathbb E\|U^i_n-V^i_n\|\longrightarrow0.$$ Suppose there are probability measures $\nu_n$ on $[-M,M]$, a constant $c>0$, and events $G^i_n\in\mathcal A^i_n$ of probability tending to one, such that, on $G^i_n$, $$\mathbb P(V^i_n\in B\mid\mathcal A^i_n)\ge c\,\nu_n(B) \quad\text{for every Borel set }B.$$ Then every subsequence has a further subsequence on which all the $U^i_n,V^i_n$ converge in probability to the same deterministic constant.
  - Explanation: Two close bounded readings with one common conditional lower measure can only have common deterministic subsequential limits.
- **claim-bounded-mean-locality** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h-locality)): Assume the sequentially uniform comparison and trace estimates of Theorem <a href="#c:comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="c:comparison">15</a> and Theorem <a href="#t:trace" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="t:trace">40</a>, and the local weak equation of Proposition <a href="#b:cell" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="b:cell">30</a>. Consider two conditioning systems with uniformly bounded mean profiles and the same lattice domain and original fixed data inside a ball of radius $R$. Suppose they share a connected oriented strand across that ball and all sign observations inside it. For averaged observations at distance of order $r$ from that strand, supported in the concentric ball of radius $R/2$, where $r\to\infty$ in lattice units and $r/R\to0$, the two conditional means differ by a quantity tending to zero.* *There is also an exterior version. If the two systems agree outside a ball of radius $\rho$, their original exterior data agree, and their unchanged strands connect that ball to radius $R$, then at distance of order $r$ from its center, with $\rho\ll r\ll R$, the limiting mean difference is at most $CM(\rho/r)^{1/2}$. Here $M$ bounds the individual profiles. In both assertions use translates and dilates of the fixed radial probability kernel from Section <a href="#sec:trace-analysis" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:trace-analysis">6</a>. A sampling ball centered at $y$ has radius $s$ less than one tenth of both $r$ and the distance from $y$ to the boundary of the common free region. For each fixed $a>0$, retain $s\ge ar$ while taking the mesh limit in coordinates rescaled by $r$; the cutoff may then decrease to zero.
  - Explanation: Common-wall traces and the weak equation make mean differences harmonic with zero local boundary trace. Beurling estimates bound the influence of distant changes in interior and exterior comparisons.
- **claim-common-absolute-boundary-readings** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h-readings)): Assume the harmonic-mean compactness and common-sign trace comparison of Proposition <a href="#b:cell" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="b:cell">30</a>, Theorem <a href="#c:comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="c:comparison">15</a>, and Theorem <a href="#t:trace" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="t:trace">40</a>. Assume also the landing exclusions <a href="#h:landing-exclusions" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h:landing-exclusions">[h:landing-exclusions]</a> and the sampled-configuration estimates of Proposition <a href="#g:sample-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="g:sample-comparison">59</a> and Lemma <a href="#g:extra" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="g:extra">60</a>. Then, along any joint subsequence of finitely many experiments, after extracting their geometric incident-edge branch probabilities as above, the following construction gives the hypotheses of Lemma <a href="#h:common-kernel" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="h:common-kernel">68</a> simultaneously for all nonvanishing branches. Its readings take values in $[0,M]$, and their limiting variables are the absolute values $\|Y\|$ of the Brownian strand-boundary samples of the conditional mean profiles. No landing-side sign is conditioned upon.
  - Explanation: Signed locality first matches canonical inner and modified outer readings to the same boundary sample. Taking absolute values afterwards permits a common lower kernel on unoriented records without conditioning on the landing sign.
- **claim-terminal-mean-side-sign** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h-terminal-sign)): For a complete crosscut in a sign-compatible Dobrushin experiment, the conditional mean at every positive-side primal vertex is nonnegative, and at every negative-side primal vertex it is nonpositive. Every limiting harmonic conditional mean has the same sign in its respective component. If $s\in\{+1,-1\}$ is the incident-side label of a Brownian strand-boundary sample $Y$, then $sY\ge0$.
  - Explanation: Freezing the completed crosscut separates the free primal components. Their incident pins have the appropriate sign, so monotonicity against a symmetric zero-pinned law fixes the sign of terminal means and their harmonic samples.
- **claim-subsequential-universal-height-gap** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h-height-gap)): Assume the uniform inputs of Proposition <a href="#h:readings" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="h:readings">70</a> and the trace bounds of Lemmas <a href="#g:sign-trace" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="g:sign-trace">52</a> and <a href="#g:upper-half" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="g:upper-half">53</a>. Every mesh subsequence has a further subsequence and a deterministic $l\in(0,1/2]$ such that all terminal conditional mean profiles in any prescribed finite collection of the sign-compatible Dobrushin experiments specified above have Brownian boundary trace $+l$ on a positive strand side and $-l$ on a negative strand side.
  - Explanation: The common absolute reading kernel yields a deterministic magnitude shared across experiments. Terminal signs and completed-reference trace bounds make the gap strictly positive and bounded.
- **claim-uniform-stopped-harmonic-observable** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h-stopped)): Fix a subsequence furnished by Proposition <a href="#h:height-gap" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="h:height-gap">72</a> and its deterministic height gap $l$. In this proposition $n$ tends to infinity only along that subsequence. Assume <a href="#h:nr" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h:nr">[h:nr]</a>, the survival bound of Lemma <a href="#g:survival" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="g:survival">63</a>, and the sequentially uniform field comparisons. Harmonic sampling and boundary marks are as in Lemmas <a href="#h:slit-sampling" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="h:slit-sampling">66</a> and <a href="#h:marked-limits" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="h:marked-limits">67</a>. Let $H^l_{n,T}$ be the continuum harmonic function in the stopped physical domain with the original exterior values and values $+l,-l$ on the new sides. For every deterministic smooth test $f$ supported in a protected interior ball, $$\label{h:stopped-observable} \sup_T\mathbb E\left\|M^n_T(f)-\int f(z)H^l_{n,T}(z)\,\mathrm dz\right\| \longrightarrow0.$$ The supremum is over stopping rules before a fixed neighborhood of that ball is reached, and the assertion holds in either direction of exploration.
  - Explanation: Survival reweighting and harmonic-mass nonreturn transfer completed height-gap traces to stopped prefixes. Marked harmonic uniqueness then identifies the conditional-mean martingale against each deterministic protected test.
- **claim-matched-observable-driving-limit** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h-driving)): For simple lattice crosscuts in marked Jordan domains, suppose that the exact conditional-mean martingales of deterministic protected interior averages satisfy <a href="#h:stopped-observable" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h:stopped-observable">[h:stopped-observable]</a>, uniformly over the stopping rules of the driving argument, with matched exterior heights $\pm l$, where $l>0$. Suppose the comparison is to the continuum slit-domain function <a href="#h:angle" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h:angle">[h:angle]</a>. Then the forward chordal drivers converge, locally uniformly in capacity time in law, to $2B$.
  - Explanation: Protected deterministic averages supply the harmonic martingale probes needed for bounded-coordinate diffusion comparison, yielding the chordal Brownian driver.
- **claim-whole-curve-uniform-convergence** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h-uniform-path)): Consider the matched height-gap subsequence above, with exterior heights $\pm l$. Assume the stopped-observable conclusion of Proposition <a href="#h:stopped" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="h:stopped">73</a> in both directions, observer avoidance <span class="upright">(GB4)</span>, harmonic-mass nonreturn <a href="#h:nr" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h:nr">[h:nr]</a>, and the harmonic sampling conclusion of Lemma <a href="#h:slit-sampling" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="h:slit-sampling">66</a>. Then the interfaces converge to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_4$ in uniform Euclidean distance modulo increasing reparametrization.
  - Explanation: Forward and reverse drivers, common terminal side labels, and harmonic-mass nonreturn identify one ordered limiting arc and exclude overlapping futures. This upgrades the limit to uniform curve convergence.
- **claim-height-gap-variance-normalization** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h-normalization)): Assume the joint conclusions of Proposition <a href="#h:stopped" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="h:stopped">73</a>, Theorem <a href="#t:covariance" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="t:covariance">42</a>, and the field limit Theorem <a href="#b:gff" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="b:gff">32</a>, with the uniform moments needed to pass conditional second moments. Then every subsequential height gap satisfies $$l^2=\frac{\pi\sigma^2}{8}.$$
  - Explanation: Total variance equates the conditional-mean martingale bracket with loss of Dirichlet Green covariance, uniquely fixing the height gap in terms of field variance.
- **claim-domain-independent-matched-amplitude** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h-assembly)): For the model of Section <a href="#sec:model" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:model">1</a>, the constant $$\lambda_*=\sigma\sqrt{\pi/8}$$ belongs to $(0,1/2]$, is independent of the marked domain, and gives the curve conclusion of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>. The field stiffness is $vA=\sigma^{-2}$, and its limiting mean is the harmonic extension of the prescribed exterior values.
  - Explanation: Variance normalization fixes the same matched amplitude on every subsequence. The field, mean, and whole-curve conclusions therefore hold without subsequence extraction.

        "anchor": "stmt-f-hole",
        "exact_quote": "Let a random bad set on the square grid satisfy <a href=\"#f:animal\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"f:animal\">[f:animal]</a> with sufficiently small parameter. Fill the bounded complementary components of each bad star-connected cluster and retain its outermost filled hulls. A fixed layer of enlargement is allowed. There is an extension procedure which, for a field $u$ on good sites, fills each hole by its value at one surrounding good site. Here good sites lie outside the filled holes and good edges join neighboring good sites. Write $v$ for the resulting field. A hole is incident to $z$ if it contains $z$ or a neighbor of $z$; let $d_z$ be the largest diameter of an incident hole, zero if none, and put $d_e=\\max(d_x,d_y)$ for $e=\\{x,y\\}$. Uniformly in deterministic $z$, $$\\label{f:hole-tail}\n \\mathbb P(d_z\\ge r)\\le Ce^{-cr}.$$ For every $1<p<2$, on a square of side $N$ with a fixed larger buffer, $$\\label{f:hole-weighted}\n \\|\\nabla v\\|_{\\ell^p}\n \\le E^{1/2}\n \\left(\\sum_e W_e^{2/(2-p)}a_e^{-p/(2-p)}\\right)^{(2-p)/(2p)},\n \\quad W_e\\le C_p(1+d_e)^{2p},$$ where $E=\\sum_{e\\text{ good}}a_e|\\nabla u(e)|^2$, $a_e>0$. In particular, bounded spatial moments of sufficiently high powers of $d_e$ and $a_e^{-1}$ imply $$\\label{f:hole-scaled}\n \\|\\nabla v\\|_{\\ell^p}\\le C N^{2/p-1}\\sqrt E.$$ If $u$ is the restriction of a globally $K$-Lipschitz field on the grid, then $|u(z)-v(z)|\\le CK(1+d_z)$.*\n\n*For every fixed $q,D<\\infty$, the spatial average of $(1+d_z)^q$ in a square of side $N$ is bounded by a deterministic constant outside an event of probability $O(N^{-D})$. In a box of side $n$, these bounds hold simultaneously on all subboxes of radius at least $n^{1/2}$, after altering the failure exponent. Filling can be chosen equivariantly under translations of the block grid. No reciprocal-weight assertion follows from sparsity alone; those moments are separate hypotheses in <a href=\"#f:hole-weighted\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"f:hole-weighted\">[f:hole-weighted]</a>.",
