      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-c-comparison",
        "exact_quote": "Consider the experiments just specified, with $|a|+|b|$ bounded. Assume the conclusions of <a href=\"#f:conditioned-sparse\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"f:conditioned-sparse\">12</a>, <a href=\"#f:hole\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"f:hole\">6</a>, and <a href=\"#f:averages\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"f:averages\">2</a> for their original marginal laws. Individual reflecting constraints are ordinary one-sided sign walls, not pairs $0\\le h_x\\le\\varepsilon$ with $\\varepsilon$ allowed to tend to zero. Fix $0<r<R<2$, $1<p<2$, and a desired defect parameter $\\rho>0$. There are fixed testing parameters, a step length $T_\\rho>0$, good edges $G_n$ and good wall sites $S_n^{\\rm g}$, and positive weights $w_e,w_x\\le1$ with the following properties.*\n\n\n\n*For either tail in <a href=\"#c:tails\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"c:tails\">[c:tails]</a>, or for their signed difference, let $$\\label{c:energy}\n \\mathcal E_n(Q)=\n \\sum_{e\\in G_n,\\ e\\subset Q}w_e|\\nabla_e u_0|^2\n +\\sum_{x\\in S_n^{\\rm g}\\cap Q}w_x|u_0(x)|^2.$$ In the two-tail statement the energies are added. In a free comparison the energy is that of $z$ and there is no wall sum. Then $$\\label{c:energy-bound}\n \\mathbb E\\mathcal E_n(Q_r)\\le C,\\qquad\n \\mathbb E\\sum_{C:\\,C\\cap Q_r\\ne\\varnothing}D_C\\le C.$$ Here $C$ and $D_C$ have the preceding step-cluster meaning. The constants in <a href=\"#c:energy-bound\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"c:energy-bound\">[c:energy-bound]</a> may depend on $\\rho,p,r,R$ and the average bounds. Defective boxes satisfy the prescribed sparse-animal bound. For every fixed $q<\\infty$ and $A<\\infty$, the normalized spatial sums of $w^{-q}$, cluster-size moments, and hole-diameter moments are bounded by deterministic constants outside an event of probability $O(n^{-A})$. The relevant finite collection of moment orders can be chosen in advance.*\n\n\n*Let $U_n$ be the extension over holes supplied by <a href=\"#f:hole\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"f:hole\">6</a>, with a fixed choice of the testing parameters. It can be set to zero on the exceptional event. In scaled coordinates, $$\\label{c:compactness}\n \\mathbb E\\|U_n\\|_{W^{1,p}(n^{-1}Q_r)}^2\\le C,\\qquad\n \\mathbb E\\int_{n,Q_r}|U_n-u_0|\\longrightarrow0.$$ In a free comparison subtract a local cutoff-weighted average from both $U_n$ and $z_0$. Its gradient and dissipation estimates are unchanged. All these centered estimates are uniform in the size of the ambient domain. The same bounds hold for a rough one-sided adapted experiment with only $z|_P\\ge a$, for $u^-=(a-z)_+$, and with zero extension behind a controlled observed boundary. They hold uniformly after replacing $z$ by $z/K$, $K\\ge1$, with bounded rescaled thresholds.*\n\n\n**Threshold-uniform specialization.* In the one-sided case, for each threshold $a$ satisfying the required condition $z|_P\\ge a$, the weights may be chosen independently of $a$. With the original marginal moment bounds fixed, $$\\label{c:threshold-scaling}\n \\mathbb E\\mathcal E_n\\bigl((a-z)_+;Q_r\\bigr)\n +\\mathbb E\\|U_n^{(a)}\\|_{W^{1,p}(n^{-1}Q_r)}^2\n \\le C_0(1+a^2).$$ Thus, when $a=K\\ge1$ and the observed values satisfy $z|_P\\ge K$, the energy and squared Sobolev norm of $(1-z/K)_+$ are bounded by $2C_0$, uniformly in $K$.*\n\n*For an ordinary simply connected polygon domain with identical fixed boundary data, the exterior-preserving construction in Lemma <a href=\"#c:exterior-zero\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"c:exterior-zero\">21</a> gives a bounded $W^{1,p}(\\mathbb R^2)$ extension which is exactly zero outside the lattice polygon. This construction uses connectivity of its zero exterior; it is not asserted for an arbitrary disconnected internal observed set.*\n\n*If $Q_R$ has no observations or individual walls, and $X_n$ is sampled from normalized ambient volume in $Q_r$, then $n\\nabla_{(X_n,X_n+\\mathbf e)}z_0$ for each fixed lattice step $\\mathbf e$, $n(z_0(X_n+i)-z_0(X_n))$ for each fixed lattice offset $i$, and $n\\sup_{t\\le T_0}|z_t(X_n)-z_0(X_n)|$ are tight. Thus this untruncated conclusion has a fixed positive macroscopic free buffer. It also holds up to controlled observations when $a=b$, because the two tails then control $z-a$. For general $a<b$, corresponding tightness statements hold only for the controlled tails up to observations. Here $T_0$ is one fixed sufficiently short step. Sampling is not conditioned on an arbitrarily small random free set.*\n\n*Finally these statements allow a drift difference bounded by $c n^{-2}$, with bounded support on the macroscopic scale, including a sufficiently small smooth exponential tilt of either marginal. Constants may depend on a fixed bound for $c$; the smallness needed for the change of marginal law is that in <a href=\"#f:averages\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"f:averages\">2</a>.",
        "source_id": "PM-232.3"
      },

In scaled coordinates, $$\\label{c:compactness}\n \\mathbb E\\|U_n\\|_{W^{1,p}(n^{-1}Q_r)}^2\\le C,\\qquad\n \\mathbb E\\int_{n,Q_r}|U_n-u_0|\\longrightarrow0.$$ In a free comparison subtract a local cutoff-weighted average from both $U_n$ and $z_0$. Its gradient and dissipation estimates are unchanged. All these centered estimates are uniform in the size of the ambient domain. The same bounds hold for a rough one-sided adapted experiment with only $z|_P\\ge a$, for $u^-=(a-z)_+$, and with zero extension behind a controlled observed boundary. They hold uniformly after replacing $z$ by $z/K$, $K\\ge1$, with bounded rescaled thresholds.*\n\n\n**Threshold-uniform specialization.* In the one-sided case, for each threshold $a$ satisfying the required condition $z|_P\\ge a$, the weights may be chosen independently of $a$. With the original marginal moment bounds fixed, $$\\label{c:threshold-scaling}\n \\mathbb E\\mathcal E_n\\bigl((a-z)_+;Q_r\\bigr)\n +\\mathbb E\\|U_n^{(a)}\\|_{W^{1,p}(n^{-1}Q_r)}^2\n \\le C_0(1+a^2).$$ Thus, when $a=K\\ge1$ and the observed values satisfy $z|_P\\ge K$, the energy and squared Sobolev norm of $(1-z/K)_+$ are bounded by $2C_0$, uniformly in $K$.*\n\n*For an ordinary simply connected polygon domain with identical fixed boundary data, the exterior-preserving construction in Lemma <a href=\"#c:exterior-zero\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"c:exterior-zero\">21</a> gives a bounded $W^{1,p}(\\mathbb R^2)$ extension which is exactly zero outside the lattice polygon. This construction uses connectivity of its zero exterior; it is not asserted for an arbitrary disconnected internal observed set.*\n\n*If $Q_R$ has no observations or individual walls, and $X_n$ is sampled from normalized ambient volume in $Q_r$, then $n\\nabla_{(X_n,X_n+\\mathbf e)}z_0$ for each fixed lattice step $\\mathbf e$, $n(z_0(X_n+i)-z_0(X_n))$ for each fixed lattice offset $i$, and $n\\sup_{t\\le T_0}|z_t(X_n)-z_0(X_n)|$ are tight. Thus this untruncated conclusion has a fixed positive macroscopic free buffer. It also holds up to controlled observations when $a=b$, because the two tails then control $z-a$. For general $a<b$, corresponding tightness statements hold only for the controlled tails up to observations. Here $T_0$ is one fixed sufficiently short step. Sampling is not conditioned on an arbitrarily small random free set.*\n\n*Finally these statements allow a drift difference bounded by $c n^{-2}$, with bounded support on the macroscopic scale, including a sufficiently small smooth exponential tilt of either marginal. Constants may depend on a fixed bound for $c$; the smallness needed for the change of marginal law is that in <a href=\"#f:averages\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"f:averages\">2</a>.",

        "exact_quote": "On a zero-drift step, normal reflection of a difference acts on each transmission cluster by compositions of averaging projections and their convex mixtures.         "anchor": "stmt-b-bulk",
        "exact_quote": "Under the inputs specified above, the gradient process and its driving Brownian increments, viewed from a uniformly sampled vertex in a compact macroscopic region separated by a fixed positive macroscopic distance from all fixed pins and reflecting sign walls, have a unique local limit. This limit is independent of the bounded boundary data and of the small smooth tilts under consideration. It is stationary in space and time and spatially ergodic. Its local trajectories are continuous and have normal reflection. On a fixed short step, every vertex belongs to a finite transmission cluster; there are almost surely no simultaneous distinct-face contacts. A face visited away from the endpoints of a contact episode has positive reflection impulse in that episode.",

      },
      "evidence": [

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-b-tangent",
        "exact_quote": "On a finite isolated cluster, consider a normal-reflection trajectory with interior endpoints, no simultaneous distinct-face contacts, and positive impulse in each visited-face episode. For two compared trajectories whose initial states are sufficiently close to the reference initial state and which use the same driving path, sufficiently close to the reference drive, their synchronous difference update is exactly a finite product $$J=P_{e_k}\\cdots P_{e_1}.$$ Consequently, if the initial relative differences multiplied by $n$ are tight, their limiting update is $w'=Jw$ modulo constants.         "anchor": "stmt-b-extraction",
        "exact_quote": "Let $z$ be a stationary comparison on scale $n$ covered by Theorem <a href=\"#c:comparison\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"c:comparison\">15</a>, with relative drift $n^{-2}b(x/n)$.         "exact_quote": "Fix an edge. Suppose that there are forward-past measurable events $G_j$ with $\\mathbb P(G_j)\\to1$.       "hypotheses": [

          "anchor": "stmt-b-controlled",
          "exact_quote": "A controlled solution of slope $q\\in\\mathbb R^2$ is a space-time stationary joining of $\\mathcal E$ with real relative heights $(w_x(k))$, defined modulo a spatial additive constant at each $k\\in\\mathbb Z$, such that:\n\n1. For every $\\delta>0$ there are spatial constants $c_R$ for which $$\\frac1{|\\Lambda\\cap B_R|}\n     \\#\\{x\\in\\Lambda\\cap B_R:\n           |w_x-q\\cdot x-c_R|>\\delta R\\}\n     \\longrightarrow0$$ in probability as $R\\to\\infty$.\n\n3.  If $C_x$ is the step cluster of $x$, $H_x=|C_x|$, and $$d_x=\\frac1{|C_x|}\\sum_{y\\in C_x}\n              \\bigl(w_y^2-(Jw)_y^2\\bigr),$$ then $\\mathbb Ed_0<\\infty$. For every fixed $a\\ge0$, $\\mathbb E[H_0^a|(Jw-w)_0|]<\\infty$.\n\nThe loss defining $d_x$ is nonnegative and invariant under addition of a constant.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-g-shifts",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-g-insertion",
        "exact_quote": "For every fixed $L<\\infty$ there is $p_L>0$ with the following property. Condition on any admissible exact oriented strands. In a patch of diameter at most $L$, at distance at most $L$ from one of their tips or from bounded Dirichlet boundary, prescribe a compatible sign pattern on at most $L$ additional vertices. The probability of that pattern is at least $p_L$. In particular every feasible prescribed extension of at most $L$ interface steps has a probability bounded below by a constant depending only on $L$. There are also absolute $p_*,b_*>0$ such that every nonfixed positive string site has conditional probability at least $p_*$ to have height greater than $b_*$, without any restriction on its distance from strand tips or Dirichlet boundary. Both assertions remain valid when other positive string sites have additional upper bounds in $(0,d]$, provided neither a prescribed new positive site nor the tested string site is one of those upper-bounded sites.",

        "anchor": "stmt-g-screened-comparison",
        "exact_quote": "Consider a one-sided experiment from Theorem <a href=\"#c:comparison\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"c:comparison\">15</a> at scale $R\\to\\infty$, after an adapted exact-value transcript has been recorded. Let $G$ be a recorded union of components of the common unqueried graph. Every original lattice edge from $G$ to its complement must end at a common fixed vertex; no free–free edge is deleted in selecting $G$. There are no unrecorded individual walls in $G$. Write $P$ for all fixed vertices incident to $G$, $z=h-\\widetilde h$, and consider either $$u=(a-z)_+,\\quad P_{\\rm c}=\\{p\\in P:z(p)\\ge a\\},\n \\qquad\\hbox{or}\\qquad\n u=(z-b)_+,\\quad P_{\\rm c}=\\{p\\in P:z(p)\\le b\\},$$ with bounded threshold. Put $P_{\\rm u}=P\\setminus P_{\\rm c}$ and define $$\\delta_G(x,P_{\\rm u})=\n \\inf\\{\\operatorname{diam}_\\infty\\gamma:\n \\gamma=(x,\\ldots,p)\\text{ is a lattice path with }\n \\gamma\\setminus\\{p\\}\\subset G,\\ p\\in P_{\\rm u}\\}.       \\tag{SC1}$$ Fixed vertices are terminal, not traversable, in (SC1), and an empty infimum is infinity.*\n\n*Let $Q_{\\rm in}\\Subset Q_{\\rm out}$ be coordinate squares fixed before the transcript is sampled, with separation comparable to $R$ and $\\operatorname{diam}_\\infty Q_{\\rm out}\\le(c_0-c_1)R$ for a fixed $c_1>0$. Suppose that a tested set $T\\subset G\\cap Q_{\\rm in}$ satisfies $\\delta_G(x,P_{\\rm u})\\ge c_0R$ for every $x\\in T$. Assume the original annealed sparse-contact, hole, and deterministic-test average hypotheses of Theorem <a href=\"#c:comparison\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"c:comparison\">15</a> in a fixed enlargement of $Q_{\\rm out}$. Use full ambient Lipschitz extensions of both marginals. In particular the negative Sobolev bound is for the full, unmasked $z$ there, including its zeroth-scale anchored average. Then the one-sided conclusions of that theorem hold on $Q_{\\rm in}$ for the components meeting $T$, with the tail extended by zero behind their controlled fixed boundary. Its hole extension $U$ satisfies, for every $1<p<2$, $$\\mathbb E\\|U\\|_{W^{1,p}(R^{-1}Q_{\\rm in})}^2\\le C,\\qquad\n \\mathbb ER^{-2}\\sum_{x\\in T}|U(x)-u(x)|\\longrightarrow0.     \\tag{SC2}$$ It is zero at retained vertices of $P_{\\rm c}$ in this window. The constants may depend on the square ratios and $c_0$. The same statement holds on a recorded event of probability at least $p_*>0$, with constants depending on $p_*$. No estimate is asserted at a test with short access to $P_{\\rm u}$. A trace application must separately verify thickness and transport to retained controlled pins; the artificial rim is not a zero-tail trace anchor.",

        "anchor": "stmt-g-sign-trace",
        "exact_quote": "In a local sector with only positive string boundary, the limiting bounded harmonic conditional mean has Brownian boundary trace at least $c>0$, away from endpoints and incompatible sides. Here a testing neighborhood has a fixed access-diameter margin, in the actual free graph after the string heights are frozen, from every incident boundary pin not controlled by the comparison below; fixed pins cannot be traversed. On a negative sector its trace is at most $-c$. On an exterior boundary arc alone the trace is its prescribed value. If the pure sector also has positive exterior pins at least $\\lambda_*>0$, its lower bound is $c\\wedge\\lambda_*$; the negative mixed sector is reflected. These statements are sequentially uniform at diverging lattice scales.",

        "exact_quote": "Fix concentric inner and outer disks with radii in a fixed ratio strictly greater than one.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-h-common-kernel",
        "exact_quote": "For $1\\le i\\le k$, let $U^i_n,V^i_n$ take values in $[-M,M]$, with $U^i_n$ measurable with respect to a sigma-field $\\mathcal A^i_n$. Suppose that $$\\mathbb E|U^i_n-V^i_n|\\longrightarrow0.$$ Suppose there are probability measures $\\nu_n$ on $[-M,M]$, a constant $c>0$, and events $G^i_n\\in\\mathcal A^i_n$ of probability tending to one, such that, on $G^i_n$, $$\\mathbb P(V^i_n\\in B\\mid\\mathcal A^i_n)\\ge c\\,\\nu_n(B)\n \\quad\\text{for every Borel set }B.$$ Then every subsequence has a further subsequence on which all the $U^i_n,V^i_n$ converge in probability to the same deterministic constant.",
        "source_id": "PM-232.3"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-h-common-kernel",
          "exact_quote": "For $1\\le i\\le k$, let $U^i_n,V^i_n$ take values in $[-M,M]$, with $U^i_n$ measurable with respect to a sigma-field $\\mathcal A^i_n$. Suppose that $$\\mathbb E|U^i_n-V^i_n|\\longrightarrow0.$$ Suppose there are probability measures $\\nu_n$ on $[-M,M]$, a constant $c>0$, and events $G^i_n\\in\\mathcal A^i_n$ of probability tending to one, such that, on $G^i_n$, $$\\mathbb P(V^i_n\\in B\\mid\\mathcal A^i_n)\\ge c\\,\\nu_n(B)\n \\quad\\text{for every Borel set }B.$$ Then every subsequence has a further subsequence on which all the $U^i_n,V^i_n$ converge in probability to the same deterministic constant.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        }
      ],
      "exact_statement": "For $1\\le i\\le k$, let $U^i_n,V^i_n$ take values in $[-M,M]$, with $U^i_n$ measurable with respect to a sigma-field $\\mathcal A^i_n$. Suppose that $$\\mathbb E|U^i_n-V^i_n|\\longrightarrow0.$$ Suppose there are probability measures $\\nu_n$ on $[-M,M]$, a constant $c>0$, and events $G^i_n\\in\\mathcal A^i_n$ of probability tending to one, such that, on $G^i_n$, $$\\mathbb P(V^i_n\\in B\\mid\\mathcal A^i_n)\\ge c\\,\\nu_n(B)\n \\quad\\text{for every Borel set }B.$$ Then every subsequence has a further subsequence on which all the $U^i_n,V^i_n$ converge in probability to the same deterministic constant.",
      "explanation": "Two close bounded readings with one common conditional lower measure can only have common deterministic subsequential limits.",
      "fidelity": "PENDING",
      "hypotheses": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-h-common-kernel",
          "exact_quote": "For $1\\le i\\le k$, let $U^i_n,V^i_n$ take values in $[-M,M]$, with $U^i_n$ measurable with respect to a sigma-field $\\mathcal A^i_n$.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-h-common-kernel",
          "exact_quote": "Suppose that $$\\mathbb E|U^i_n-V^i_n|\\longrightarrow0.$$",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-h-common-kernel",
          "exact_quote": "Suppose there are probability measures $\\nu_n$ on $[-M,M]$, a constant $c>0$, and events $G^i_n\\in\\mathcal A^i_n$ of probability tending to one, such that, on $G^i_n$, $$\\mathbb P(V^i_n\\in B\\mid\\mathcal A^i_n)\\ge c\\,\\nu_n(B)\n \\quad\\text{for every Borel set }B.$$ Then every subsequence has a further subsequence on which all the $U^i_n,V^i_n$ converge in probability to the same deterministic constant.*\n\n</div>\n\n<details id=\"proof-stmt-h-common-kernel\"><summary>Proof of stmt-h-common-kernel</summary>\n\n*Proof.* Pass to a subsequence on which $\\nu_n$ and the laws of all $U^i_n$ converge. Conditional integration gives $$\\mathbb E|U^i_n-V^i_n|\n \\ge c\\,\\mathbb E\\left[\\mathbf1_{G^i_n}\n          \\int|U^i_n-y|\\,\\nu_n(\\,\\mathrm dy)\\right].$$ The lost contribution outside $G^i_n$ is at most $2M\\mathbb P((G^i_n)^c)$. If $\\mu_i$ and $\\nu$ are the limiting laws, bounded continuity yields $\\int|x-y|\\,\\mu_i(\\,\\mathrm dx)\\nu(\\,\\mathrm dy)=0$. A product of two probability measures supported on the diagonal must consist of the same point mass in each coordinate. The point is common to all $i$ because $\\nu$ is common. Agreement of the readings completes the proof. ◻\n\n</details>\n\nThe constant $c$ in this lemma need not approach one. It must, however, stay positive as unused scale buffers grow. A different reference law for each external configuration would not provide the stated conclusion.\n\n\n<div id=\"h:locality\" class=\"lemma\">\n\n**Lemma 69** (Locality of bounded conditional means). *Assume the sequentially uniform comparison and trace estimates of Theorem <a href=\"#c:comparison\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"c:comparison\">15</a> and Theorem <a href=\"#t:trace\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"t:trace\">40</a>, and the local weak equation of Proposition <a href=\"#b:cell\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"b:cell\">30</a>. Consider two conditioning systems with uniformly bounded mean profiles and the same lattice domain and original fixed data inside a ball of radius $R$. Suppose they share a connected oriented strand across that ball and all sign observations inside it. For averaged observations at distance of order $r$ from that strand, supported in the concentric ball of radius $R/2$, where $r\\to\\infty$ in lattice units and $r/R\\to0$, the two conditional means differ by a quantity tending to zero.*\n\n*There is also an exterior version. If the two systems agree outside a ball of radius $\\rho$, their original exterior data agree, and their unchanged strands connect that ball to radius $R$, then at distance of order $r$ from its center, with $\\rho\\ll r\\ll R$, the limiting mean difference is at most $CM(\\rho/r)^{1/2}$. Here $M$ bounds the individual profiles. In both assertions use translates and dilates of the fixed radial probability kernel from Section <a href=\"#sec:trace-analysis\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:trace-analysis\">6</a>. A sampling ball centered at $y$ has radius $s$ less than one tenth of both $r$ and the distance from $y$ to the boundary of the common free region. For each fixed $a>0$, retain $s\\ge ar$ while taking the mesh limit in coordinates rescaled by $r$; the cutoff may then decrease to zero.*\n\n</div>\n\n<details id=\"proof-stmt-h-locality\"><summary>Proof of stmt-h-locality</summary>\n\n*Proof.* For the first assertion compare the two fields with common reflecting sign walls. On shared strands their limiting mean difference has zero Brownian-tested trace by the comparison and trace estimates. The common original fixed data give zero differences at the corresponding pins, so the same trace argument gives zero trace on the common original boundary pieces. Away from these observed boundaries the difference is harmonic by the weak equation and $A>0$. Its absolute value on the other boundary pieces is at most $2M$. The maximum principle therefore bounds it by $2M$ times the probability of escaping the common ball before hitting the connected common strand. Beurling bounds that probability by $C(r/R)^{1/2}$. For arbitrary sequences with $r\\to\\infty$ and $r/R\\to0$, rescale by $r$ and first restrict to a common ball of radius $Lr$ about a nearest strand point, with $L$ fixed. Centrality puts this ball inside the shared region for all sufficiently large scales. Local $L^1$ compactness transfers its $CM L^{-1/2}$ bound to the fixed-cutoff averages. First take the mesh limit, then $L\\to\\infty$, and finally remove the averaging cutoff. Sequential uniformity gives the assertion for every admissible conditioning sequence.\n\nFor the second assertion apply the identical argument in the common exterior region, with the small changed window as the only uncontrolled boundary. The probability of reaching that window from distance $r$ before hitting a connected common arm is at most $C(\\rho/r)^{1/2}$. The bounds persist under averaging in a sufficiently small ball about the observation point. In both assertions the zero trace is a conclusion of the common-wall comparison, not an equality of the sampled wall heights. ◻\n\n</details>\n\n\n<div id=\"h:readings\" class=\"proposition\">\n\n**Proposition 70** (The two absolute readings required for the height gap). *Assume the harmonic-mean compactness and common-sign trace comparison of Proposition <a href=\"#b:cell\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"b:cell\">30</a>, Theorem <a href=\"#c:comparison\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"c:comparison\">15</a>, and Theorem <a href=\"#t:trace\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"t:trace\">40</a>. Assume also the landing exclusions <a href=\"#h:landing-exclusions\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"h:landing-exclusions\">[h:landing-exclusions]</a> and the sampled-configuration estimates of Proposition <a href=\"#g:sample-comparison\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"g:sample-comparison\">59</a> and Lemma <a href=\"#g:extra\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"g:extra\">60</a>. Then, along any joint subsequence of finitely many experiments, after extracting their geometric incident-edge branch probabilities as above, the following construction gives the hypotheses of Lemma <a href=\"#h:common-kernel\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"h:common-kernel\">68</a> simultaneously for all nonvanishing branches. Its readings take values in $[0,M]$, and their limiting variables are the absolute values $|Y|$ of the Brownian strand-boundary samples of the conditional mean profiles. No landing-side sign is conditioned upon.*\n\n</div>\n\n<details id=\"proof-stmt-h-readings\"><summary>Proof of stmt-h-readings</summary>\n\n*Proof.* Regard each nonvanishing event $E_{n,\\sigma}$ as one member of the finite collection; independence between these members is not needed. If none remain, the assertion about strand samples is vacuous. Work under each branch’s conditional law, disintegrated over the landing location and translated as above. We use the resulting $Z^\\sigma$ notation, always with the landing sign still averaged. The actual orientation remains part of each signed conditional mean. We construct auxiliary signed inner and outer readings $\\widetilde V_n,\\widetilde U_n$ which approximate the same signed boundary sample. Their absolute values will be the readings $V_n,U_n$. The inner absolute reading, unlike its signed auxiliary version, will be a function of the unoriented record and so will admit the common lower comparison from (G7).\n\nFor a target error, first use <a href=\"#h:landing-exclusions\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"h:landing-exclusions\">[h:landing-exclusions]</a> to discard strand landings within distance $\\eta d_n$ of the original boundary or observer, choosing $\\eta>0$ so that their probability is small. Recenter a retained landing at zero. Choose the lattice radii $$1\\ll r_{\\rm in}\\ll R_{\\rm core}\\ll R_{\\rm in}\\ll R_{\\rm mid}\n       \\ll R_{\\rm conn}\\ll r_{\\rm out}\\ll n.                 \\tag{H1}$$ Require also $r_{\\rm out}<\\eta d_n/20$. Thus the disk $\\mathfrak B_{12R_{\\rm in}}$ used by (G7) and the disks $\\mathfrak B_{4R_{\\rm in}}$, $\\mathfrak B_{4R_{\\rm conn}}$ used by (G8) lie inside the original domain and exclude the observer. Clearance is measurable in the outer record, which includes the domain and observer; retaining it imposes no additional condition on the inner strand. Write $\\mathcal A_n=\\sigma(\\Phi_{R_{\\rm mid}})$ under this side-unconditioned $Z^\\sigma$ mixture, and let $G_n\\in\\mathcal A_n$ be the retained clearance event. The diagonal choices below make $\\mathbb P(G_n)\\to1$.\n\n*Agreement of complete-profile readings.* First take mesh limits at fixed positive physical approach distances. In each limiting component the bounded harmonic martingale has a boundary limit. Its values at first entrances into balls of radii tending to zero about the eventual landing have that same limit: these entrance times approach the exit time pathwise. They need not be stopping times after the future-dependent center is specified.\n\nAt an interior approach point use a radial smooth average in a ball smaller than one tenth of its distance to the strand and of the approach radius, with the fixed probability kernel defining $P_s$ in Section <a href=\"#sec:trace-analysis\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:trace-analysis\">6</a>. The limiting harmonic average equals the value at its center. Impose a positive lower cutoff on the averaging radius before taking the mesh limit, then remove it. At each fixed positive physical approach scale the sampling point is interior almost surely, so this cutoff loses arbitrarily little probability. The comparison compactness and the vanishing original–filled $L^1$ error give convergence of the conditional means in $L^1$ on every compact subset of the limiting free regions, on a joint subsequential realization. At a fixed radius cutoff $a>0$, the sampling supports have distance at least $9a$ from the strand; the retained landing clearance and (H1) also keep them a fixed positive distance from the original exterior. Hausdorff convergence therefore places all these supports in one compact subset $C_a$ of the limiting free regions. Since the kernels have supremum norm at most $\\|\\varphi\\|_\\infty a^{-2}$, the discrepancy of their readings is bounded uniformly by $\\|\\varphi\\|_\\infty a^{-2}\\|m_n-m\\|_{L^1(C_a)}$, which tends to zero. This transfers both readings to the lattice, including for kernels selected from the records. Denote the signed complete-profile readings at $r_{\\rm in}$ and $r_{\\rm out}$ by $B_n^{\\rm in}$ and $B_n^{\\rm out}$, assigning zero when their kernel cutoff fails. Such failures have vanishing probability. A diagonal choice of the radii in (H1) makes both readings converge in $L^1$ to $Y$ on the joint subsequential realization, and in particular $\\mathbb E|B_n^{\\rm in}-B_n^{\\rm out}|\\to0$. These statements hold under the side-unconditioned branch law: the bounded errors under the original sampling law are divided only by the branch’s positive probability lower bound. The scales are chosen slowly; no convergence rate is asserted.\n\n*The reading determined by the inner record.* Write $\\theta=(\\beta,w)$ for the unoriented record $\\Theta_{R_{\\rm in}}$. An admissible connected incident strand through $e_\\sigma^*$ has exactly two lifts to adjacent sign observations: choosing the sign at the landing vertex $0$ propagates the signs along the nonbranching strand. Denote by $o_+(\\theta)$ the lift for which $0$ is positive, and by $o_-(\\theta)$ its sign reversal. This deterministic choice of a lift only defines an auxiliary function of $\\theta$; it does not condition the sampled field on that sign.\n\nFor $o\\in\\{o_+,o_-\\}$, let $m^{\\rm can}_{\\theta,o}$ be the conditional mean in the centered rounded disk of radius $2R_{\\rm in}$, with zero exterior heights and precisely the strand signs in $o$. Choose the rounding equivariantly under the six lattice rotations. These polytopes have positive volume: assign small heights $+b$ and $-b$ to their respective string sites and zero to the other free sites, with $0<b<1/2$. All free edge inequalities and sign inequalities are then strict. The volume-preserving map $h\\mapsto-h$ exchanges the two canonical polytopes and fixes the zero exterior data. Consequently $$m^{\\rm can}_{\\theta,o_-}(z)=-m^{\\rm can}_{\\theta,o_+}(z)\n \\quad\\text{at every }z.                                      \\tag{H1a}$$\n\nApply (G8) at $(R_{\\rm core},R_{\\rm in})$ and average its conditional bound. Except on an event of vanishing probability under $Z^\\sigma$, the walk does not leave $R_{\\rm in}$ after its first entrance at $R_{\\rm core}$. Its first entrance at $r_{\\rm in}$ therefore belongs to the recorded terminal piece, and reversing that piece determines the sampling point. Any complete-chord piece in $B(0,R_{\\rm core})$ other than the incident strand $\\beta_{R_{\\rm in}}^\\sigma$ would give two additional crossings of the same annulus. Outside the same type of exceptional event, the canonical conditioning with the actual oriented lift and the complete conditioning thus agree throughout $B(0,R_{\\rm core})$.\n\nChoose the inner radial kernel using the distance to the recorded geometric strand and the cutoff just described; denote it by $\\kappa_\\theta$. Both its center and its radius are functions only of $\\theta$. For a valid approach point and cutoff put $$v_{n,o}(\\theta)\n   =\\int\\kappa_\\theta(z)m^{\\rm can}_{\\theta,o}(z)\\,\\mathrm dz,\n \\qquad\n F_n(\\theta)=|v_{n,o_+}(\\theta)|.$$ If the record has no admissible incident strand, does not contain the required approach point, or fails the kernel cutoff, set both $v_{n,o}$ and $F_n$ equal to zero. These fallback rules are geometric. Equation (H1a) gives $v_{n,o_-}=-v_{n,o_+}$, including the fallback cases. Thus $$V_n:=F_n(\\Theta_{R_{\\rm in}})\n       =|\\widetilde V_n|,\n \\qquad\n \\widetilde V_n:=v_{n,o_{\\rm actual}}(\\Theta_{R_{\\rm in}}).\n                                                        \\tag{H1b}$$ The inner record space is countable, and the lift, kernel, and fallback choices are deterministic. Hence $V_n$ is one bounded measurable function of the unoriented record, the same in every experiment, and does not use $G_n$. The absolute value is taken after testing an oriented canonical mean; averaging the two orientations before taking the absolute value would instead give zero and is not the construction.\n\nApply Lemma <a href=\"#h:locality\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"h:locality\">69</a> to each actual oriented conditioning, with $r_{\\rm in}/R_{\\rm core}\\to0$. Its sequential uniformity allows these errors to be averaged over the actual orientations under $Z^\\sigma$. The extra-excursion estimate supplies both the common strand neighborhood and the presence of the chosen approach point in the recorded walk. Boundedness absorbs its exceptional events and the cutoff failures, so $$\\mathbb E|B_n^{\\rm in}-\\widetilde V_n|\\longrightarrow0.$$ No landing sign has been conditioned on in this expectation.\n\n*The reading determined by the outer record.* Retain the external arms and initial walk in $\\Phi_{R_{\\rm mid}}$. Delete every oriented dual-edge observation whose adjacent primal sign pair meets $B(0,R_{\\rm conn})$; retain the remaining external-arm edge observations and both vertices of each pair. Every retained sign vertex still has an oppositely constrained neighbor.\n\nApply (G8) at $(R_{\\rm mid},R_{\\rm conn})$ and average its bound. Except on an event of vanishing probability under $Z^\\sigma$, the unrecorded connection of the two external arms stays inside $B(0,R_{\\rm conn})$: the arms already supply two disjoint annular crossings, and an excursion of their connection would supply two more. Hence the modified and complete conditionings agree outside $B(0,R_{\\rm conn}+C)$, with an absolute lattice constant $C$. All retained observations are determined by $\\Phi_{R_{\\rm mid}}$. The first walk entrance at $r_{\\rm out}$ is also in that record, since it precedes the first entrance at $R_{\\rm mid}$.\n\nUse a radial kernel smaller than one tenth of $r_{\\rm out}$ and of the distance to the recorded external strands, with a positive lower cutoff as above. Its support stays outside the changed window. The mean under the modified conditioning, tested with this kernel, is $\\mathcal A_n$-measurable, since that record includes the oriented external-arm observations; denote this signed reading by $\\widetilde U_n$. Set $\\widetilde U_n=0$ when its required outer clearance or kernel cutoff fails, and put $U_n=|\\widetilde U_n|$. In the common exterior component, limiting mean differences are bounded harmonic functions with zero trace on the unchanged strands and original boundary. The only uncontrolled boundary is the deleted window, where the difference has absolute value at most $2M$. A connected common arm crosses the intervening annulus. The maximum principle and Beurling’s estimate therefore bound the influence of this window at the sampling ball by $$C M(R_{\\rm conn}/r_{\\rm out})^{1/2}.$$ The bounded enlargement by $C$ is negligible at these scales. Sequentially uniform compactness and trace comparison transfer the bound to the lattice with an error tending to zero. After including the bounded exceptional contributions, this gives $\\mathbb E|\\widetilde U_n-B_n^{\\rm out}|\\to0$. The inequality $\\bigl||a|-|b|\\bigr|\\le |a-b|$ now gives $$\\mathbb E|U_n-V_n|\n \\le \\mathbb E|\\widetilde U_n-B_n^{\\rm out}|\n     +\\mathbb E|B_n^{\\rm out}-B_n^{\\rm in}|\n     +\\mathbb E|B_n^{\\rm in}-\\widetilde V_n|\n \\longrightarrow0.                                      \\tag{H1c}$$ All three errors are integrated under the side-unconditioned branch law. In particular the absolute value is taken only after the signed locality and harmonic-mean arguments.\n\n*One common lower kernel and the order of limits.* Fix a geometric edge label $\\sigma_0$. Write $F_{n,\\sigma}$ for the function just constructed in branch $\\sigma$, and let $T_\\sigma$ be the lattice rotation fixing $0$ and carrying $e_\\sigma^*$ to $e_{\\sigma_0}^*$. The zero exterior canonical disk, the lift making $0$ positive, the radial kernel, and every fallback rule commute with this rotation. A spatial change of variables therefore gives $$F_{n,\\sigma}(\\theta)\n       =F_{n,\\sigma_0}(T_\\sigma\\theta).                  \\tag{H1d}$$ For each sufficiently large $n$, choose one admissible reference external record $\\phi_n^*$ at radius $4R_{\\rm in}$ with label $\\sigma_0$ and positive hookup probability. Such a record can be taken from any nonvanishing branch after its outer clearance and a rotation: the clearance probability tends to one, and the discrete record space is countable. Let $\\nu_n$ be the law on $[0,M]$ obtained by pushing $$\\operatorname{Law}_*(\\Theta_{R_{\\rm in}}\\mid\n             \\Phi_{4R_{\\rm in}}=\\phi_n^*,Z^{\\sigma_0})$$ through $F_{n,\\sigma_0}$.\n\nFor any fine external record $\\phi$ in branch $\\sigma$ with positive hookup probability and satisfying the disk hypotheses of (G7), rotate the experiment by $T_\\sigma$ and apply the orientation-averaged (G7) to the event $\\{F_{n,\\sigma_0}(\\Theta_{R_{\\rm in}})\\in B\\}$. Equation (H1d) yields $$\\mathbb P(F_{n,\\sigma}(\\Theta_{R_{\\rm in}})\\in B\n       \\mid\\Phi_{4R_{\\rm in}}=\\phi,Z^\\sigma)\n       \\ge C^{-1}\\nu_n(B)                                \\tag{H1e}$$ for every Borel set $B$.",

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Uniform real Lipschitz height law** ([source](#eq:model)): For $0<\lambda\le1/2$, let $h_\delta$ have normalized Lebesgue measure on the set of real vertex heights satisfying $$\label{eq:model} h_\delta=\lambda\text{ on }A_{+,\delta},\qquad h_\delta=-\lambda\text{ on }A_{-,\delta},\qquad \|h_\delta(x)-h_\delta(y)\|\le1\quad(x\sim y).$$
- **Riemann pairing** ([source](#sec:conventions)): Continuum tests use the Riemann pairing $$\langle h,f\rangle_n=\frac1{vn^2}\sum_x f(x/n)h_x.$$
- **Convex-good block** ([source](#f:near)): For fixed $0<\delta\le\delta_0\le1/16$, an integer $k_0\ge4/\delta_0$, and $s_0>0$, call a block *convex-good* for $h$ if $$\begin{aligned} \|h(x)-h(y)\|&\le1-\delta &&(x\sim y\text{ in }Q),\label{f:near}\\ \|h(x)-h(y)\|&\le(1-\delta_0)\operatorname{dist}(x,y) &&(x,y\in Q,\ \operatorname{dist}(x,y)\ge k_0),\label{f:far} \end{aligned}$$ and the following four non-tie conditions hold. For each face center $v$, take the radial coordinate path from $v$ to the block center. Exactly one ray on its starting face has compressed triangular distances to that path; if $b_1$ is its first vertex, require $\|h(b_1)-h(v)\|\ge s_0$.
- **Controlled tangent solution** ([source](#stmt-b-controlled)): A controlled solution of slope $q\in\mathbb R^2$ is a space-time stationary joining of $\mathcal E$ with real relative heights $(w_x(k))$, defined modulo a spatial additive constant at each $k\in\mathbb Z$, such that: 1. The relative heights form a spatial cocycle: after choosing $w_0=0$, they obey $w_{x+y}-w_x=w_y\circ\tau_x$, where $\tau_x$ shifts the joined environment and relative field by $x$. They update by $w(k+1)=J_k w(k)$ modulo constants. 2. For every $\delta>0$ there are spatial constants $c_R$ for which $$\frac1{\|\Lambda\cap B_R\|} \#\{x\in\Lambda\cap B_R: \|w_x-q\cdot x-c_R\|>\delta R\} \longrightarrow0$$ in probability as $R\to\infty$. 3. If $C_x$ is the step cluster of $x$, $H_x=\|C_x\|$, and $$d_x=\frac1{\|C_x\|}\sum_{y\in C_x} \bigl(w_y^2-(Jw)_y^2\bigr),$$ then $\mathbb Ed_0<\infty$. For every fixed $a\ge0$, $\mathbb E[H_0^a\|(Jw-w)_0\|]<\infty$. The loss defining $d_x$ is nonnegative and invariant under addition of a constant. A slope is called attained if such a solution exists.
- **Cluster-averaged tangent flux** ([source](#b:flux-definition)): For a controlled solution define the cluster-averaged flux at $x$ by $$\label{b:flux-definition} \mathcal J_x(w)= -\frac1{T\|C_x\|}\sum_{y\in C_x}(y-\overline C_x)(Jw-w)_y, \qquad \overline C_x=\frac1{\|C_x\|}\sum_{y\in C_x}y.$$
- **Continuum thickness of an observed set** ([source](#stmt-t-thickness)): A compact set $K\subset\overline Q$ containing $\partial Q$ has *continuum thickness below $r_0$* if, for each $x\in K$ and $0<r<r_0$, there is a compact connected set $$x\in L\subset K\cap\overline B(x,2r),\qquad \operatorname{diam}L\ge r.$$ For mesh approximants the same condition is required only for $c/n\le r<r_0$, with fixed $c$. All uniform assertions about a family of observed sets use common constants $c,r_0$.
- **Frostman testing measures and zero trace** ([source](#stmt-t-frostman-definition)): For $0<\alpha\le1$ and $M<\infty$, let $\mathcal M_\alpha(M)$ consist of positive measures supported in $\overline Q$ satisfying $$\mu(\overline Q)\le M,\qquad \mu(B(x,r))\le Mr^\alpha\quad(0<r\le1).$$ The statement that a Sobolev function has zero $\alpha$-Frostman trace on $K$ means that its trace vanishes in $L^1(\mu)$ for every $\mu\in\bigcup_{M<\infty}\mathcal M_\alpha(M)$ supported on $K$.
- **Threshold-averaged feasible shift** ([source](#eq:shift-prescription)): For $s\in[s_0,s_1]$, let $C_s(x)$ be the component of $x$ using edges with $t_e(h)\leq s$, and define $$v_s(h)_x= \begin{cases} \|C_s(x)\|^{-1}\displaystyle\sum_{y\in C_s(x)}f_y, & C_s(x)\hbox{ has no grounded vertex},\\ 0, & C_s(x)\hbox{ has a grounded vertex}. \end{cases} \qquad u(h)=\Delta^{-1}\int_{s_0}^{s_1}v_s(h)\,ds.$$

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-local-volume-and-sparse-slack** [claim](#stmt-f-block) / [proof](#proof-stmt-f-block): Expose triangular facets, apply quantitative slice log-concavity, and telescope centroid increments. Controlled-gradient witnesses and non-tie marginal bounds then give sparse bad blocks. -> Block deficit and zero-pinned sparse-block estimates.
- **step-hole-traces-and-average-coercivity** [claim](#stmt-f-hole) / [proof](#proof-stmt-f-hole): Fill holes from good rims, use weighted path inequalities, and test against spread measures to remove additive constants. -> Sparse-hole extension, spread-measure trace bounds, and uniform average coercivity.
- **step-macroscopic-moments-and-bounded-data** [claim](#stmt-f-averages) / [proof](#proof-stmt-f-average-coercivity-2): Integrate block interiors, convert midpoint volume deficits into overlap loss, and use log-concavity for exponential tails. Monotone heat baths transfer the estimate to bounded data. -> Uniform exponential moments for admissible averages and bounded-data mixtures.
- **step-tilts-sign-filling-and-tightness** [claim](#stmt-f-conditioned-sparse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-f-conditioned-sparse): Use exponential moments for small tilts, cone extensions and homothetic contractions for sign-compatible slack, and forward–reverse displacement control for short-step persistence. Haar cancellation gives negative Sobolev tightness. -> Small-tilt transfer, strict filling, conditioned sparsity, stationary persistence, and distributional tightness.
- **step-adapted-kernels-and-cluster-projections** [claim](#stmt-c-freezing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-c-freezing): Disintegrate adapted query transcripts, preserve annealed marginals under invariant joinings, transfer conditional exceptional bounds, and differentiate polytope projections. -> Correct conditional Gibbs laws, sparse conditional failures, and cluster displacement controlled by square loss.
- **step-force-and-insulate** [claim](#stmt-c-force) / [proof](#proof-stmt-c-force): Reduce difference constraints to genuine facet paths, construct stable reflected forcing tubes on a compact parameter family, and isolate them with quiet exterior shells. -> Uniform positive impulse opportunities outside sparse insulation failures.
- **step-local-energy-and-zero-exterior** [claim](#stmt-c-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-c-exterior-zero): Allocate forced losses without cluster overcounting, combine cutoff estimates with average absorption, remove filling errors through improved good parameters, and select zero exterior rim anchors. -> Local reflected comparison, controlled-tail compactness, microscopic tightness, and an exterior-preserving extension.
- **step-bulk-law-and-tangent-extraction** [claim](#stmt-b-bulk) / [proof](#proof-stmt-b-bulk): Compare with independent reference boxes, extract local gradient-and-driver laws, identify regular finite reflection products, and recover affine growth from filled stationary gradients. -> Unique ergodic bulk environment, stable tangent updates, and controlled volume-sampled tangent solutions.
- **step-contact-recurrence-and-uniqueness** [claim](#stmt-b-zero-slope) / [proof](#proof-stmt-b-zero-slope): Pass finite forcing inequalities to the unmarked forward filtration, use conditional recurrence to connect contacts, and eliminate zero-slope dissipation by stationary truncated convex loss. -> Forward contact connectivity and spatial constancy of zero-slope controlled solutions.
- **step-flux-and-positive-response** [claim](#stmt-b-cell) / [proof](#proof-stmt-b-cell): Join same-slope solutions over their environment, use uniqueness and lattice symmetries for scalar flux, pass stationary cluster first moments to a weak equation, and test a positive source with zero trace. -> Well-defined isotropic flux, positive stiffness, Dirichlet mean response, and the harmonic untilted mean.
- **step-gaussian-field-law** [claim](#stmt-b-gff) / [proof](#proof-stmt-b-gff): Differentiate logarithmic moment generating functions under small smooth tilts, integrate the limiting response, and combine Gaussian test laws with distributional tightness and affine-pairing control. -> Centered Dirichlet Gaussian free field limit with the identified variance.
- **step-varying-traces-and-poisson-uniqueness** [claim](#stmt-t-trace) / [proof](#proof-stmt-t-trace): Construct averaged Frostman traces, transport testing mass along thick continua, bound retained anchor errors, and use Brownian approach measures to identify the variational Poisson solution. -> Zero traces on varying observed sets and Poisson uniqueness including positive-area observed parts.
- **step-conditional-covariance-and-local-variance** [claim](#stmt-t-covariance) / [proof](#proof-stmt-t-covariance): Identify tilted responses by zero-trace uniqueness, pass conditional moment generating functions and Green forms to limits, transfer only through exact kernels, and compare with bounded auxiliary domains near observed continua. -> Uniform deterministic and random-string covariances, Green continuity, and ambient-uniform local boundary variance decay.
- **step-volume-controlled-feasible-shifts** [claim](#stmt-g-shifts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-g-shifts): Average prescriptions over threshold components, prove facet tangency, compare determinant coefficients, and restrict to configurations with controlled cluster size and derivative norms. -> Feasible injective shifts retaining uniformly positive image probability.
- **step-insertion-screening-and-side-traces** [claim](#stmt-g-sign-trace) / [proof](#proof-stmt-g-sign-trace): Insert bounded local signs by contraction, retain full recorded free components for one-sided comparisons, and compare pure-side pins with fair bounded pin mixtures. Completed-crosscut symmetry supplies the upper bound. -> Local insertion, screened pin comparison, positive pure-side trace, and complete-crosscut mean bounds.
- **step-high-crossings-and-barrier-fences** [claim](#stmt-g-barriers) / [proof](#proof-stmt-g-barriers): Contradict persistent high crossings using normalized tails and continuum traces. Exhaustive attachment exploration, local variance decay, and feasible shifts then create connected strict sign fences. -> Uniform avoidance of compatible straight-attachment barriers.
- **step-strand-hookup-and-sampled-records** [claim](#stmt-g-sample-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-g-sample-comparison): Swap isolated dependency components across free annuli, construct separated hookup corridors, and iterate smaller-separation growth–collapse rounds before normalizing by logarithmic hookup probabilities. -> Exact-strand comparison, hookup bounds, harmonic-landing separation, comparable sampled records, and exclusion of additional excursions.
- **step-clearance-survival-and-nonreturn** [claim](#stmt-g-nonreturn) / [proof](#proof-stmt-g-nonreturn): Use pure-arc repulsion and full-walk exits for boundary clearance, nested shields for observer avoidance, and survival reweighting to pass completed excursion bounds to stopped landings. -> Boundary and observer clearance, positive survival probabilities, and stopping-rule-uniform harmonic-mass nonreturn.
- **step-labelled-sampling-and-common-readings** [claim](#stmt-h-readings) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h-readings): Couple walk and Brownian exits in physical slits, retain conformal boundary marks, prove signed locality, and take absolute readings only after matching canonical inner and modified outer profiles. -> Label-preserving harmonic sampling, marked limits, locality, and a common lower kernel for absolute boundary readings.
- **step-reference-height-gap-and-stopped-observable** [claim](#stmt-h-stopped) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h-stopped): Use the common reading kernel for a deterministic magnitude, complete-crosscut monotonicity for its sign, and reference trace bounds for positivity. Survival and nonreturn transfer the terminal trace to stopped profiles. -> A subsequential universal positive height gap and the uniform stopped harmonic observable in both exploration directions.
- **step-drivers-and-whole-curve** [claim](#stmt-h-uniform-path) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h-uniform-path): Apply the protected-average martingale criterion to both drivers, identify their common terminal side labels, exclude overlapping futures by harmonic-mass nonreturn, and recover ordered uniform convergence. -> Matched-boundary driver convergence and whole-curve convergence in the uniform metric.
- **step-gap-normalization-and-main-assembly** [claim](#stmt-h-normalization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h-normalization): Compare total variance with the harmonic-observable bracket and conformal Green loss. The resulting unique gap removes subsequence dependence and assembles the field and interface limits. -> Universal tuned amplitude, field stiffness, harmonic mean, and the main theorem.

          "exact_quote": "Let a random bad set on the square grid satisfy <a href=\"#f:animal\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"f:animal\">[f:animal]</a> with sufficiently small parameter. Fill the bounded complementary components of each bad star-connected cluster and retain its outermost filled hulls. A fixed layer of enlargement is allowed. There is an extension procedure which, for a field $u$ on good sites, fills each hole by its value at one surrounding good site. Here good sites lie outside the filled holes and good edges join neighboring good sites. Write $v$ for the resulting field. A hole is incident to $z$ if it contains $z$ or a neighbor of $z$; let $d_z$ be the largest diameter of an incident hole, zero if none, and put $d_e=\\max(d_x,d_y)$ for $e=\\{x,y\\}$. Uniformly in deterministic $z$, $$\\label{f:hole-tail}\n \\mathbb P(d_z\\ge r)\\le Ce^{-cr}.$$ For every $1<p<2$, on a square of side $N$ with a fixed larger buffer, $$\\label{f:hole-weighted}\n \\|\\nabla v\\|_{\\ell^p}\n \\le E^{1/2}\n \\left(\\sum_e W_e^{2/(2-p)}a_e^{-p/(2-p)}\\right)^{(2-p)/(2p)},\n \\quad W_e\\le C_p(1+d_e)^{2p},$$ where $E=\\sum_{e\\text{ good}}a_e|\\nabla u(e)|^2$, $a_e>0$. In particular, bounded spatial moments of sufficiently high powers of $d_e$ and $a_e^{-1}$ imply $$\\label{f:hole-scaled}\n \\|\\nabla v\\|_{\\ell^p}\\le C N^{2/p-1}\\sqrt E.$$ If $u$ is the restriction of a globally $K$-Lipschitz field on the grid, then $|u(z)-v(z)|\\le CK(1+d_z)$.*\n\n*For every fixed $q,D<\\infty$, the spatial average of $(1+d_z)^q$ in a square of side $N$ is bounded by a deterministic constant outside an event of probability $O(N^{-D})$. In a box of side $n$, these bounds hold simultaneously on all subboxes of radius at least $n^{1/2}$, after altering the failure exponent. Filling can be chosen equivariantly under translations of the block grid. No reciprocal-weight assertion follows from sparsity alone; those moments are separate hypotheses in <a href=\"#f:hole-weighted\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"f:hole-weighted\">[f:hole-weighted]</a>.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },

          "anchor": "stmt-f-trace-average",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\nu$ be a positive measure of bounded mass in a square of side $O(N)$, and assume $\\nu(B(x,r))\\le C((r+1)/N)^\\alpha$ for $0\\le r\\le CN$. If $1<p<2$ and $\\alpha>2-p$, then $$|\\nu(v)-\\nu(1)\\overline v|\n \\le C N^{1-2/p}\\|\\nabla v\\|_{\\ell^p},$$ where $\\overline v$ is the ordinary average over that square.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-f-average-coercivity",
          "exact_quote": "Suppose $X$ is globally $K$-Lipschitz on the block grid, with fixed $K$. Suppose either $u=X$, or $u=T_M(X)$ for fixed $T_M(t)=\\operatorname{sign}(t)(|t|-M)_+$. Let $E=\\sum_{e\\text{ good}}|\\nabla u(e)|^2$. For deterministic weights $w$ supported in an $O(N)$ square with $\\sum|w|\\le C$ and $\\max|w|\\le CN^{-2}$, assume either $\\sum w=0$, or $u=0$ on a connected deterministic coarse pin set of diameter comparable to $N$ at distance $O(N)$. There is an event of probability at least $1/2$, determined only by the bad set, on which simultaneously for every such field $X$, $$\\label{f:coercivity}\n \\left|\\sum_z w_zX_z\\right|\\le C_0+C_1\\sqrt E.$$",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        }

          "exact_quote": "Consider the experiments just specified, with $|a|+|b|$ bounded. The constants in <a href=\"#c:energy-bound\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"c:energy-bound\">[c:energy-bound]</a> may depend on $\\rho,p,r,R$ and the average bounds.           "exact_quote": "Under the inputs specified above, the gradient process and its driving Brownian increments, viewed from a uniformly sampled vertex in a compact macroscopic region separated by a fixed positive macroscopic distance from all fixed pins and reflecting sign walls, have a unique local limit.       "evidence": [

          "anchor": "stmt-b-cell",
          "exact_quote": "Under the preceding inputs, $j(q)$ is well defined on the vector space of attained slopes and is linear there. If any nonzero slope is attained, every slope in $\\mathbb R^2$ is attained and $j(q)=Aq$ for a finite scalar $A$. For a stationary comparison with drift difference $n^{-2}b(x/n)$, every subsequential expected macroscopic difference $m$ satisfies $$\\label{b:weak-equation}\n \\int j(\\nabla m)\\cdot\\nabla f=\\int b f,\n \\qquad f\\in C_c^\\infty(U),$$ in each limiting open region $U$ free of observations.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-b-response",
          "exact_quote": "Assume the comparison and average estimates hold up to identical fixed boundaries of lattice domains converging to a bounded smooth domain $D$. Then every slope is attained and the scalar in Proposition <a href=\"#b:cell\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"b:cell\">30</a> satisfies $0<A<\\infty$. For sufficiently small smooth sources $b$, the mean response to relative drift $n^{-2}b(x/n)$ converges to $$A^{-1}(-\\Delta_D)^{-1}b.$$ For boundary values $+\\lambda$ and $-\\lambda$ on the two marked arcs, the untilted mean converges to their bounded harmonic extension.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        }
      ],

          "anchor": "stmt-t-trace",
          "exact_quote": "Let $K\\subset\\overline Q$ contain $\\partial Q$ and have continuum thickness below $r_0$. Let $3/2<p<2$, $A>0$, and $b\\in L^\\infty(Q)$. Then, on $Q$, $$\\label{t:poisson-identification}\n u=A^{-1}G_Vb,$$ where the right side is extended by zero on $K$. In particular the restriction of $u$ to $V$ belongs to $H^1_0(V)$.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-t-frostman",
          "exact_quote": "Let $1<p<2$, $0<\\alpha\\le1$, and $p+\\alpha>2$. Every $u\\in W^{1,p}(Q^*)$ has a trace $T_\\mu u\\in L^1(\\mu)$ for $\\mu\\in\\mathcal M_\\alpha(M)$, and $$\\label{t:trace-rate}\n \\int|T_\\mu u-P_ru|\\,\\mathrm d\\mu\n \\le C r^\\beta\\|\\nabla u\\|_{L^p(Q^*)},\\qquad\n \\beta=1-\\frac{2-\\alpha}{p}>0.$$ The constant is uniform over $\\mathcal M_\\alpha(M)$.*\n\n\n\n*For a piecewise affine mesh function $u_n$, suppose instead that a measure on mesh vertices satisfies $$\\label{t:coarse-frostman}\n \\mu_n(B(x,r))\\le C(r+\\ell_n/n)^\\alpha,\n \\qquad \\mu_n(\\overline Q)\\le C,$$ where $1\\le\\ell_n\\le C(\\log n)^C$. Then, for fixed $r>0$, $$\\label{t:mesh-trace-rate}\n \\int|u_n-P_ru_n|\\,\\mathrm d\\mu_n\n \\le C\\left(r^\\beta+\n       \\ell_n^{\\alpha/p}n^{-\\beta}\\right)\n       \\|\\nabla u_n\\|_{L^p(Q^*)}.$$",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-t-transport",
          "exact_quote": "Suppose $K$ has continuum thickness below $r_0$. If $\\mu\\in\\mathcal M_\\alpha(M)$ is supported within distance $\\eta$ of $K$, where $0<\\eta<r_0/10$, there is a measure $\\nu\\in\\mathcal M_\\alpha(CM)$ supported on $K$ and a coupling $\\pi$ of $\\mu,\\nu$ supported on $|x-y|\\le C\\eta$. Consequently $$\\label{t:transport-trace}\n \\int|T_\\mu u(x)-T_\\nu u(y)|\\,\\mathrm d\\pi(x,y)\n \\le C\\eta^\\beta\\|\\nabla u\\|_p$$ under the exponent assumptions of Lemma <a href=\"#t:frostman\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"t:frostman\">35</a>.*\n\n*If mesh sets $K_n$ have the common thickness constants and converge to $K$ in Hausdorff distance, every such measure supported on $K$ is the weak limit of continuous measures in $\\mathcal M_\\alpha(CM)$ supported on $K_n$. For geometric mesh graphs, these may additionally be projected onto their vertices, giving the common bound $C(r+n^{-1})^\\alpha$.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-t-anchors",
          "exact_quote": "Let $q>1$, and let $S_n$ be retained observed vertices with positive weights $w_x$. Suppose $$\\sum_{x\\in S_n}w_x|z_x|^2\\le E_n,\n \\qquad n^{-2}\\sum_{x\\in S_n}w_x^{-q}\\le C_q.$$ For a probability measure $\\mu_n$ on these vertices with $a_n=\\max_x\\mu_n(\\{x\\})$, $$\\label{t:anchor-rate}\n \\sum_x\\mu_n(\\{x\\})|z_x|\n \\le C_q E_n^{1/2}n^{1/q}a_n^{(1+1/q)/2}.$$ In particular, if $a_n\\le C(\\ell_n/n)^\\alpha$, the bound tends to zero in expectation when $\\sup_n\\mathbb EE_n<\\infty$ and $q>(2-\\alpha)/\\alpha$. The deterministic inverse-weight bound may hold outside exceptional events, provided their contributions to the displayed quantities tend to zero.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-t-varying-trace",
          "exact_quote": "Let $K_n$ have the mesh thickness property with common constants and converge in Hausdorff distance to $K$. Let their mesh vertices carry random values $z_n$, and let $U_n$ be random piecewise affine extensions on $Q^*$. Fix $3/2<p<2$. Assume the following bounds, uniformly in $n$:*\n\n1.  *$\\mathbb E\\|U_n\\|_{W^{1,p}}\\le C$, and the means $\\mathbb EU_n$ have a subsequence converging strongly in $L^p$ to $u$;*\n\n2.  *every vertex on $K_n$ can be moved to a retained vertex on $K_n$ within distance $\\ell_n/n$, where $\\ell_n\\le C(\\log n)^C$;*\n\n3.  *$U_n=z_n$ at retained vertices, and their values satisfy Lemma <a href=\"#t:anchors\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"t:anchors\">37</a> for some $q>3$, with $\\mathbb EE_n\\le C$;*\n\n4.  *exceptional events in these assertions have vanishing contribution to the Sobolev, anchor, and fixed-scale averaged quantities used here.*\n\n\n*Then $u$ has zero $1/2$-Frostman trace on $K$ and is zero Lebesgue-almost everywhere on $K$. If the original interpolated values also satisfy $$\\label{t:original-filled}\n \\mathbb E\\|z_n-U_n\\|_{L^1(Q)}\\longrightarrow0,$$ then the original mean responses have the same distributional limit, including for smooth tests whose supports meet $K$.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"

          "anchor": "stmt-t-exit",

          "anchor": "stmt-t-covariance",
          "exact_quote": "Suppose the class $\\mathcal S_n$ and the estimates <a href=\"#t:input-moments\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"t:input-moments\">[t:input-moments]</a>–<a href=\"#t:input-flux\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"t:input-flux\">[t:input-flux]</a> hold, and set $\\sigma^2=(vA)^{-1}$. In particular, $$\\label{t:uniform-covariance}\n \\sup_{s\\in\\mathcal S_n}\\sup_{f,g\\in\\mathcal C}\n \\left|\\operatorname{Cov}_{n,s}(X_{n,s}(f),X_{n,s}(g))\n       -\\sigma^2\\langle f,G_{V_{n,s}}g\\rangle\\right|\n \\longrightarrow0.$$ There is no requirement that $K$ have zero area or that the test supports be disjoint from $K$.",

The same assertion holds for mesh-thick approximants.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-t-random-covariance",
          "exact_quote": "Let $S_n$ take values in $\\mathcal S_n$, and suppose $$\\label{t:kernel}\n \\operatorname{Law}(h_n\\mid S_n=s)=P_{n,s}\n \\quad\\hbox{for almost every }s.$$ Then, for fixed tests or compact families as in Theorem <a href=\"#t:covariance\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"t:covariance\">42</a>, the conditional covariance differs in $L^1$ from $\\sigma^2\\langle f,G_{V_{n,S_n}}g\\rangle$ by $o(1)$. If $K_{n,S_n}$ converges in distribution to $K$, these random Green forms converge in distribution and in expectation to those on $Q\\setminus K$.           "anchor": "stmt-t-boundary-variance",
          "exact_quote": "Let $K$ satisfy Definition <a href=\"#t:thickness\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"t:thickness\">33</a> and let $V=Q\\setminus K$.         {
          "anchor": "stmt-t-local-boundary-variance",
          "exact_quote": "Fix nested squares $Q_0\\Subset Q_1\\Subset Q_2\\Subset Q_3$ and positive geometric separation constants. This holds for connected strands attached to the original exterior, or for components of uniformly positive diameter: cut pieces meeting the artificial boundary join that boundary, and pieces entirely inside are whole original components.*\n\n\n*For each fixed $\\eta>0$, let $\\mu_{n,\\eta}$ be a deterministic smooth probability test supported in $Q_0$, at distance at most $C\\eta$ from the observed set in $Q_1$.       "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-g-sign-trace",
          "exact_quote": "In a local sector with only positive string boundary, the limiting bounded harmonic conditional mean has Brownian boundary trace at least $c>0$, away from endpoints and incompatible sides. Here a testing neighborhood has a fixed access-diameter margin, in the actual free graph after the string heights are frozen, from every incident boundary pin not controlled by the comparison below; fixed pins cannot be traversed. On a negative sector its trace is at most $-c$. On an exterior boundary arc alone the trace is its prescribed value. If the pure sector also has positive exterior pins at least $\\lambda_*>0$, its lower bound is $c\\wedge\\lambda_*$; the negative mixed sector is reflected. These statements are sequentially uniform at diverging lattice scales.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-g-insertion",
          "exact_quote": "For every fixed $L<\\infty$ there is $p_L>0$ with the following property. Condition on any admissible exact oriented strands. In a patch of diameter at most $L$, at distance at most $L$ from one of their tips or from bounded Dirichlet boundary, prescribe a compatible sign pattern on at most $L$ additional vertices. The probability of that pattern is at least $p_L$. In particular every feasible prescribed extension of at most $L$ interface steps has a probability bounded below by a constant depending only on $L$. There are also absolute $p_*,b_*>0$ such that every nonfixed positive string site has conditional probability at least $p_*$ to have height greater than $b_*$, without any restriction on its distance from strand tips or Dirichlet boundary. Both assertions remain valid when other positive string sites have additional upper bounds in $(0,d]$, provided neither a prescribed new positive site nor the tested string site is one of those upper-bounded sites.",
          "source_id": "PM-232.3"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-g-screened-comparison",
          "exact_quote": "Consider a one-sided experiment from Theorem <a href=\"#c:comparison\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"c:comparison\">15</a> at scale $R\\to\\infty$, after an adapted exact-value transcript has been recorded. Let $G$ be a recorded union of components of the common unqueried graph. Every original lattice edge from $G$ to its complement must end at a common fixed vertex; no free–free edge is deleted in selecting $G$. There are no unrecorded individual walls in $G$. Write $P$ for all fixed vertices incident to $G$, $z=h-\\widetilde h$, and consider either $$u=(a-z)_+,\\quad P_{\\rm c}=\\{p\\in P:z(p)\\ge a\\},\n \\qquad\\hbox{or}\\qquad\n u=(z-b)_+,\\quad P_{\\rm c}=\\{p\\in P:z(p)\\le b\\},$$ with bounded threshold. Put $P_{\\rm u}=P\\setminus P_{\\rm c}$ and define $$\\delta_G(x,P_{\\rm u})=\n \\inf\\{\\operatorname{diam}_\\infty\\gamma:\n \\gamma=(x,\\ldots,p)\\text{ is a lattice path with }\n \\gamma\\setminus\\{p\\}\\subset G,\\ p\\in P_{\\rm u}\\}.       \\tag{SC1}$$ Fixed vertices are terminal, not traversable, in (SC1), and an empty infimum is infinity.*\n\n*Let $Q_{\\rm in}\\Subset Q_{\\rm out}$ be coordinate squares fixed before the transcript is sampled, with separation comparable to $R$ and $\\operatorname{diam}_\\infty Q_{\\rm out}\\le(c_0-c_1)R$ for a fixed $c_1>0$. Suppose that a tested set $T\\subset G\\cap Q_{\\rm in}$ satisfies $\\delta_G(x,P_{\\rm u})\\ge c_0R$ for every $x\\in T$. Assume the original annealed sparse-contact, hole, and deterministic-test average hypotheses of Theorem <a href=\"#c:comparison\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"c:comparison\">15</a> in a fixed enlargement of $Q_{\\rm out}$. Use full ambient Lipschitz extensions of both marginals. In particular the negative Sobolev bound is for the full, unmasked $z$ there, including its zeroth-scale anchored average. Then the one-sided conclusions of that theorem hold on $Q_{\\rm in}$ for the components meeting $T$, with the tail extended by zero behind their controlled fixed boundary. Its hole extension $U$ satisfies, for every $1<p<2$, $$\\mathbb E\\|U\\|_{W^{1,p}(R^{-1}Q_{\\rm in})}^2\\le C,\\qquad\n \\mathbb ER^{-2}\\sum_{x\\in T}|U(x)-u(x)|\\longrightarrow0.     \\tag{SC2}$$ It is zero at retained vertices of $P_{\\rm c}$ in this window. The constants may depend on the square ratios and $c_0$. The same statement holds on a recorded event of probability at least $p_*>0$, with constants depending on $p_*$. No estimate is asserted at a test with short access to $P_{\\rm u}$. A trace application must separately verify thickness and transport to retained controlled pins; the artificial rim is not a zero-tail trace anchor.",

        },

          "anchor": "stmt-g-barriers",
          "exact_quote": "Fix $\\theta>0,m<\\infty,a>0$, and for mixed layouts fix $\\kappa>0$. <a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-model-and-tuned-limit**: Uniform real Lipschitz heights on the triangular lattice have a Dirichlet Gaussian free field limit after centering and normalization; the interface limit uses the tuned boundary amplitude identified through the tangent-flux coefficient.
- **invariant-annealed-marginal-preservation**: Adapted exact-value observations permit replacement of the conditional product kernels by a stationary synchronous coupling while preserving each annealed marginal. Estimates inherited this way remain averaged over the actual transcript.
- **invariant-projection-dissipation**: Cluster displacement is controlled by square dissipation because the reflected difference evolves through averaging projections and coordinate contractions. Conserving mass alone does not supply this control.
- **invariant-thick-set-dirichlet-response**: A distributional Poisson response with the prescribed Sobolev regularity and zero Frostman trace on a thick observed set equals the Dirichlet Green response, including its zero extension on the observed set.
- **invariant-random-conditioning-kernel**: Uniform covariance estimates for deterministic sign-string kernels transfer to random strings only when those kernels are the actual conditional laws. Convergence in probability on a common probability space is additionally needed for the stated convergence in mean to a limiting random Green form.
- **invariant-whole-curve-identification**: Uniform convergence of the whole interface requires the matched height gap, stopped observables in both exploration directions, observer avoidance, harmonic-mass nonreturn, and harmonic sampling with incident accesses retained.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-closed-form-calibration**: Assign an elementary numerical stiffness or boundary amplitude directly from the scaling theorem. -> The stiffness depends on an implicit stationary tangent-flux coefficient; the theorem does not provide an elementary evaluation or a finite calibration error bound.
- **anti-use-pointwise-field-values**: Interpret distributional field convergence as tightness or convergence of individual vertex heights. -> The field conclusion concerns smooth test pairings and random distributions; it supplies no pointwise height limit.
- **anti-use-arbitrary-revealed-pins**: Apply strict filling and quenched sparse-contact estimates uniformly after arbitrary exact heights have been revealed. -> Revealed values can violate the fixed-pin range required by strict filling. Marginal preservation yields annealed estimates and does not establish a uniform bound for every transcript.
- **anti-use-shrinking-reflecting-intervals**: Extend the uniform reflected forcing argument to sign sites confined in arbitrarily thin reflecting intervals. -> Uniform initial edge slack does not provide the full-dimensional forcing construction for shrinking two-sided walls.
- **anti-use-arbitrary-random-string-selection**: Apply deterministic conditional covariance estimates to any field-dependent choice of an observed string. -> Selection can change the conditional height law; membership of the selected geometry in the reference class does not identify its conditional kernel.
- **anti-use-driver-convergence-alone**: Deduce ordered uniform curve convergence from endpoint driver convergence alone. -> Driver limits alone do not exclude macroscopic backtracking or identify the common limiting arc in the required order.
- **anti-use-untuned-interface-amplitude**: Use the chordal interface conclusion at an arbitrary boundary amplitude. -> The interface identification uses exterior heights matched to the height gap, whose value is subsequently fixed by conditional covariance.
- **anti-use-unqualified-feasible-shifts**: Treat the feasible-shift construction as a sampler or as an unconditional crossing guarantee. -> Its probability transfer starts from a measurable event with probability bounded below and retains only a subevent. The construction alone does not establish that initial crossing event.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The selected result is an asymptotic field and interface scaling limit, rather than a finite input-output construction that can be decided by test vectors. Its normalization depends on a stationary cell problem: “The stiffness is $vA$; no elementary closed form for it is proposed.” The finite feasible-shift construction is an intermediate probability-transfer argument under sparse-box hypotheses; checking finite examples would not certify the scaling limit, its implicit coefficient, or its stopping-rule uniformity.

They do not depend on $n$. Choose fixed $0<s_0<s_1<s_2<s_*$, and put $\\Delta=s_1-s_0$. For an edge $e=xy$, put $t_e(h)=1-|h_x-h_y|$. For $s\\in[s_0,s_1]$, let $C_s(x)$ be the component of $x$ using edges with $t_e(h)\\leq s$, and define $$v_s(h)_x=\n \\begin{cases}\n  |C_s(x)|^{-1}\\displaystyle\\sum_{y\\in C_s(x)}f_y,\n       & C_s(x)\\hbox{ has no grounded vertex},\\\\\n  0,   & C_s(x)\\hbox{ has a grounded vertex}.\n \\end{cases}\n \\qquad\n u(h)=\\Delta^{-1}\\int_{s_0}^{s_1}v_s(h)\\,ds.$$ Set $u=0$ outside the local graph.
